PROLOGUE
	It is autumn, 2015. The world stands on the brink - undone by events decades in the making.

	In 1908, President Theodore Roosevelt made the monumental decision to seek a third term. He won that election in a landslide - his Second Square Deal reforms streamlined the American government, empowering the executive. Satisfied, he stood down at the 1912 election, and Woodrow Wilson took the reins of power.

	Then, in 1914, a Serbian man shot an Austrian archduke. When the War began, several in the Kaiser's court suggested an invasion of Belgium to get around French defenses - but Chancellor Hollweg vetoed the plan. However, by 1916, the stalemate led to a change in tactics, and the plan was approved.
	Almost as soon as German boots crossed into Liege, the British government announced its declaration of war. American businessmen grinned unanimously, making a fortune selling guns and munitions to the Entente.
	1918 was a tumultuous year. Russia had fallen, with fighting between Socialist forces and reactionary remnants. A mutiny among French soldiers led to a new Revolution - the Second Paris Commune was born.
	Yet at the same time, the Ottoman Empire fell to the Arab revolt. American soldiers landed in the trenches of Saint-Mihel, and began to turn the tide against the German juggernaut.

	By 1920, an exhausted continent signed the Treaty of Versailles. The Spartacist Revolt came close to putting Germany on a path of socialist liberation, but was thwarted by American-funded Freikorps.
	Then, in a mansion in Gorki in 1924, Vladimir Lenin breathed his last. He was succeeded by a troika of Nikolai Bukharin, Leon Trostky, and Grigory Zinoviev. Josef Stalin, and his Bonapartist clique, were ousted - but his cronies began the work of infiltrating the state apparatus.
	In the Middle East, the colonial Sykes-Picot agreement was never signed. Instead, a pan-Arab Hashemite kingdom emerged from the ruins of the Ottoman Empire. 

	Meanwhile in American politics, Huey Long became a rising star in the Democratic Party. Supporting the New Deal, he posed a challenge to FDR - "Give me power, or I'll run against you."
	The revelation of the Business Plot by General Smedley Butler only solidified FDR's concerns about the right. When Long's popularity soared even higher following his miraculous suvival of an assasination attempt, he relented, and in the 1936 election, made Butler the Secretary of War, and Long his Secretary of State and unnofficial co-president.

	Come 1939, Spain's civil war ended in Communist victory, Germany and Italy were ruled by Hitler and Mussolini, and Britain adopted a pseudo-fascist government headed by Edward VIII - the Empire supported the Axis in opposition to Communist expansion.
	Germany, smelling blood, invaded Poland.

	The German onslaught seemed unstoppable. Fascist thugs massed outside Moscow, Leningrad, Crimea - but the Battle of Volgograd turned the tide. The American entry to the war only confirmed the inevitable - the Axis was doomed.

	In 1946, President Henry Wallace and Chairman Nikolai Bukharin shook hands in the ashes of a post-nuclear Berlin. Britain, having been cowed into submission by American brawn, watched in horror as its Empire collapsed. India declared independence in 1948, but was plagued by constant revolts in the Punjab and Bangladesh, demanding an independent Islamic state.

	Friendliness between the two superpowers soured with the ascension of Richard Nixon in 1960. Backed by the resentful oligarchs who Wallace and Long had taken turns punching, he made it his mission to contain a socialist bloc that stretched from Madrid to Seoul.
	Europe fractured: France, Spain, and much of the East aligned with Moscow, while Britain built a rival coalition of anti-communist states in northern Europe - the European Democratic Union.

	In 1962, the Hashemite Kingdom of Arabia fell to Ba'athist revolutionaries. Religious and ethnic tensions still smouldered underneath, suppressed by the watchful eye of the Party.

	China, guided by the moderate Zhang Lan after Mao's quiet ouster, threw its lot in with the Soviets. Nixon never went to China, and as it industrialised, the Soviet bloc seemed unstoppable. Even India and Arabia quietly bowed to the communist juggernauts.

	Ireland remained under British rule. A second Independence War led to devolution for Connaught, Leinster, and Munster - collectively known as the Autonomy. Ulster, however, was still ruled straight from London, with gerrymandering allowing the Protestant minority to hold a majority of power. The Troubles never ended. The Catholic provinces had substantial Loyalist minorities, imported over by the Brits after ethnic cleansing during WW2. No Irish state could be born without mass-terrorism from its Loyalist subjects - a fifth column, and a hallmark of British imperial strategy: Divide and Rule.

	Come 1994, Chairman Mikhail Gorbachev was ousted in a soft coup by Marshal Dimitry Avalov. At long last, Stalin's progeny had taken the throne. The simmering rot in the Soviet state had reached its top, and Avalov's cronies soon enriched themselves, becoming no different to the oligarchs on America they decried.
	The rest of the Soviet Bloc embraced this change, and Bonapartist leaders took power across Eurasia. In Poland, General Jaruzelski declared martial law, outlawing strikes and crushing dissent. In the Balkans, leaders like Milosevic and Boban took power in regional republics, claiming ethnic loyalty over class solidarity.
	Socialists across the globe were horrified at this shift, while separatist movements and religous extremists chafed under centralised rule.

	On the other side of the Cold War, the capitalist nations pursued reactionary politics to divide their working class. Apartheid carried on alive and well in South Africa. Australia became a brutal police state, propping up puppet states in Papua and Indonesia, as well as annexing New Zealand. In the States, the Civil Rights Act of 1957 was still on the books, but was swiftly undermined by crypto-racist policies that restored segregation in all but name.

	In 2002, mass uprisings in Derry escalated into the brutal "Bogside War." Loyalist paramilitaries, openly backed by the British state, bombed schools and massacred civilians. Britain's authoritarian grip only tightened in the aftermath - an inevitability of colonialism coming home to roost.
	Ulster Catholics decided their time was up. They emigrated - either southwards to the Autonomy, or further out to Italy.

	And then, in 2009, Eurasia fell into anarchy. Continued instability, growing nationalist movements, and the assasination of Avalov by rebels caused the mighty USSR to collapse. Its satellites followed suit - Poland came under a fundamentalist Catholic Junta, the Balkan Federation collapsed into a practical race war, and China fell into a familiar era of warlord cliques - Xinjiang, Tibet, Manchuria, Qinghai, and a weakened central remnant.

	By 2015, Britain and the United States stand as hollowed-out powers - right-wing kleptocracies where politics is theatre, wealth is power, and resistance is futile.
	
	The world is on the verge of a new, horrifying order.
	Earth is a land of decaying empires and failed states, rotten to the core.

	The old world is dying. The new world struggles to be born.

	Now is the time of monsters.

	The room was dark. An older man, with grey hair and a cropped beard, was illuminated by a blue screen that flickered into white. Ink-black veins jutted and tore from his eyesockets down his cheeks, like running mascara. His irises were a pale grey.
	"Gentlemen." he began. His accent was from the southern US, and at once sounded like honey and sulphur. "Thank you for taking the time to attend this meeting."
	"You've got a lot of nerve, Captain." a voice growled from the speakers. It was heavily modulated. Implacable.
	"It's just a temporary setback. That yellow bastard will-"
	"Enough. What's done is done." cut in a second voice. An older, upper-class accent was palpable. Even with modulation, you could hear the intonations of aristocracy. "What matters now is finding Dr. Zhou, and reminding him of his... obligations."
	"Oh, he will be reminded alright... I can assure you of that, sir." the Captain replied.
	"Good."
	"Captain?" the first voice chimed in. A hint of glee cut through the modulation.
	"Yes, sir?"
	"You are hereby ordered to cease all activities regarding the Progeny investigation."
	"...Sir." the Captain reluctantly growled.

SCENE
	The room was bright. The sun shone in through the curtainless window, illuminating a studio apartment. On the sofa-bed laid a young man with scruffy dark-blonde hair and a ginger stubble-beard. His name was Connor Barrett. His phone, plugged into a charger on the floor and resting on the arm of the sofa, began to hum a pleasant-sounding tune.
	Connor groaned, and sat up, pulling the blanket off of him. He turned off the alarm, looked down at his cushion-pillow, and seriously considered saying "Fuck it," and staying home.
	Nevertheless, he forced himself to rise. He stretched out, and it felt like every joint in his body clicked at once. In truth, just his shoulders and knees.
	He leant forward, stretching out his back and touching his toes.
	"Fuck me..." he muttered, before making himself a coffee. His accent had a funny quality - it was never sure where it was from. It sounded like it was from Devon, but had strong Irish influences as well.
	He sipped it, and allowed the bitter taste to snap him into reality. He sniffed at his armpit, and grimaced, before heading into the bathroom, stripping, and hopping into the shower.
	Hopping wasn't hyperbole - fully awake, he vaulted the bathtub's side and used his toes to soften his descent. He grinned at his own lameness.
	The hot--well, lukewarm--water flowed over his skin, washing away the sweat and the stink. He reached for the shower gel, and focused on the important bits - hair, armpits, groin. He vigorously rubbed a spot on his arm, only for the sleep-dust in his eyes to clear, and he realised it was just his freckles. He chuckled.
	As he cleaned his armpits, he bent his arm, and took a look at the tattoo on his shoulder. It was a big tribal tattoo of a wolf's head - the snout reached into the corner of his chest, and lines jolted down from his shoulder to his bicep. He grinned.
	Clean now, he left the bathroom, and buffeted himself with a towel.
	He looked at his reflection in the mirror. His steel-grey eyes caught the flickering ceiling light. He pulled his cheek with his hand, inspecting his stubble. He shrugged, content with its length. He brushed his hair, parting it with his left hand.
	He pulled out a drawer from under the sofa-bed, and put on some fresh clothes. He picked up his phone, and checked the notifications.
	A text from Missy - a picture of a particularly cute Staffy pup. "Looks just like Stella, doesn't it?" the caption read. Connor smirked.
	He checked his rota. He saw he'd be on shift with Trey, and let out a silent cheer. Sufficiently motivated, he pulled his jacket over him, put on his baseball cap, and left the flat.

If the metabolism is running that high, you're talking about the body needing *so much* energy to sustain itself. 	It would have been some time in autumn 2007. Little Connor was running through the fields. A small grey Staffy ran by his heels.
	"Come on, Stella!" Connor cheered. Stella barked back happily.
	The two leaped over a stream, and continued sprinting.
	Then, Connor was an adult again, in a kevlar bodysuit, running, with a great black wolf at his side.
	"WE'RE GETTING OUT OF HERE!" Connor roared to the wolf.
	"THEY'RE GAINING ON US!" the wolf shouted back, in perfect English.
	A group of men were chasing them. Connor looked around, confused, before he found himself back with Stella all those years ago.
	"Stella?"
	She tilted her head at Connor, wagging her little tail at him.
	Connor looked around, bewildered, and he shifted back again.
	The men chasing him had caught up. They launched bolas at Connor and the wolf, knocking both down.
	"Targets secure!" a man shouted into his radio.
	The wolf slipped out of his netting, as did Connor. The wolf launched at the men, mauling them.
	"GO!" the wolf shouted.
	"NO! I'M NOT LEAVING YOU!" Connor barked back, before a bullet buried itself into his abdomen.
	The two were overpowered, and dragged away.

	Suddenly, Connor woke up from this in a cold sweat. Blood dripped from his nose, and he clutched his blanket.
	"What the fuck happened to me..." he whispered to himself.

SCENE
	Chloe was sat in her university classroom, taking notes on her laptop.
	The professor, Isaac Rawlings, began his lecture.
	If you asked someone to draw a kindly professor, they would draw Rawlings. He was an old man, probably in his late 60's - and clearly, one who enjoyed teaching enough to stick it out for this long. His hair was unkempt, like Einstein - and his glasses, slightly too big for his face, clashed in a funny way with his small bow-tie.
	"So, class - H. I. V." he said, underlining each letter. "A true scourge of modern medicine. Our greatest weapon - the vaccine - powerless! Or, so we think."
	He smiled, and looked over the classroom.
	"I want you all to try and figure out how we could make a vaccine for HIV."
	Chloe looked up, confused. The rest of the class began writing away, or talking to each other. Chloe nervously walked over to Rawlings, who had sat down at his desk - clearly happy to have stumped the class.
	"Um, excuse me, Professor Rawlings?" she asked, sheepishly.
	"Yes, Miss Derrington?" he replied, smiling warmly.
	"Um... Well, I'm a little confused - HIV is so dangerous because it targets the immune system itself - a vaccine wouldn't do anything - would it?"
	"Indeed!" he chuckled. "Don't worry, Miss Derrington - the point of this excercise is not to break biology itself. I just want to see how you all think!"
	Chloe smiled, and nodded. "Right, of course - sorry to bother you."
	"Not at all - it's what they pay me for!" he laughed. Chloe returned to her desk, and thought deeply - googling, writing notes, and chewing her pencil absentmindedly.
	After 30 minutes had passed, Rawlings stood, and clapped his hands together, startling her.
	"Okay, class! Let's hear it. Who'd like to go first?"
	The room fell silent. Finally, one man stood up.
	"I've got an idea." he said.
	"Excellent!" Rawlings smiled. "Let's hear it!"
	"Okay, so I think we just do what we did with cowpox vs. smallpov - introduce Simian Immunodeficiency Virus into the host, and get them to base their immunity off of that." he said confidently.
	Rawlings smiled, trying to avoid looking patronising. "Well, Mr. Darvill, that's an interesting idea. Unfortunately, current understanding is that SIV-infected bushmeat was the initial cause of HIV. So, by implementing your idea, we may end up just making a new strain of HIV instead. But, A for effort!"
	He was trying hard to seem supportive. "Anyone else?"
	"Um, I have an idea!" one girl raised her hand.
	"Go ahead, Miss Ross!" Rawlings smiled.
	"Well, how about we take HIV virions, and deactivate them, before injecting the dead virions?" she asked.
	"Ah..." Rawlings pinched the bridge of his nose, trying his best to not seem rude. "Well Miss Ross, that is the standard way to induce immunity via vaccination. Unfortunately, HIV does not work with that method. HIV is unique because, unlike many other viruses, it requires a very specific interaction with immune cells - particularly T cells - to trigger an effective immune response. Simply using a dead virus may not stimulate a strong enough immune response, especially one that targets the virus effectively. And, live HIV is incredibly mutable. Anyone else?"
	Chloe's heart raced. She knew her answer was solid, but the thought of being wrong in front of everyone made her stomach churn. Still, she raised her hand.
	"Ah, yes, Miss Derrington?" Rawlings asked, smiling.
	"Ah, well, sir... Um..." Chloe fumbled over her notes. She could hear quiet snickering in the background, but steeled herself.
	"I was thinking... HIV envelopes have specific conserved regions, yes? Regions that are unlikely to mutate without making the virus unviable?"
	"Go on?" Rawlings asked, intrigued.
	"Well, those conserved regions would have antigens, right? And, well, antigens have antibodies matching them. I'm thinking, we introduce only those conserved region antigens, along with a bunch of matching monoclonal antibodies. Doing so, hopefully the body could learn to produce those antibodies. If that worked, you would only need to take ART maybe, only weekly or monthly? That'd be a godsend for people in more developing countries. Of course, the challenge would be isolating the conserved antigens and ensuring the monoclonal antibodies are broadly neutralising across HIV strains..." she continued.
	Darvill muttered under his breath "That's not a vaccine."
	Chloe paused, trembling.
	"Miss Derrington..." Rawlings began, awestruck. "Absolutely brilliant!"
	Chloe breathed a deep sigh of relief, and allowed herself a smile.
	"Amazing!" he continued. "That is a very good idea. You not only provoke an immune response, but actively improve care outcomes for the people in most need."
	Chloe smiled, and returned to her seat. Once the lecture finished, she grabbed her bag and went to leave, along with everyone else.
	"Oh, Chloe?" Rawlings asked.
	"Sir?" Chloe replied, nervous.
	"Do you have a minute?"
	"Yes, of course." Chloe smiled, sitting down.
	"I've been giving it some thought - I think it's a waste having you in this classroom." he said.
	"I... Sorry, sir, I know the objective was to come up with a vaccine idea rather than treatment, but I just thought--" Chloe began.
	Rawlings raised his hand. "Oh no, dear - your idea there was brilliant. No, I fear *you're* wasted in this lecture hall! You're far beyond the rest of the class."
	"Sir?" Chloe asked, still timid.
	"Have you ever heard of a company called 'Morland Industries'?" Rawlings asked.
	"I... Yes, sir, I've heard of them. Their head office is in Belson, isn't it?" she replied, unsure.
	"I'm going to put in the good word, and see if we can get you a work placement there." Rawlings smiled.
	"You will?" Chloe gasped. "Sir, I... Morland's such a big, successful company - are you sure I'd be any good there?"
	"Absolutely." Rawlings nodded. "The placement would be for three days a week. Working there will count towards your academic credits here, as well. And, you'll get paid!"
	"Sir, I..." Chloe thought for a moment. "I'd be honoured." she smiled.
	"Excellent." Rawlings smiled back. "Take care now, Miss Derrington."

SCENE
	That night, in Belson, a group of men in neo-nazi leathers were rifling through some boxes. A man in a military uniform oversaw them.
	"And this'll make us like you?" one of the men asked.
	"More than that." the uniformed man replied. Bulging black veins jotted his eye sockets, and a swastika armband adorned his shirt. "It'll bring our leader's vision to this mulatto city."
	Suddenly, the sound of glass shattering was heard. One of the Neo-nazis drew out his knife. "Who's there?!"
	Then the lights cut out.
	There was the sound of punching, before the man in the uniform pulled out a flashlight and gazed upon their assailant - a man in a black hoodie, black joggers, a balaclava, and black combat boots. Connor.
	The uniformed man didn't hesitate. He stepped forward, swinging. Connor dodged, but just barely, the punch grazing his ribs. His eyes widened behind the balaclava. This one is different. Superhuman.
	The two collided, fists flying with such force that each swing sliced the air audibly.
	The man in uniform matched Connor's speed and ferocity, their blows rattling the room.
	Connor blocked a punch, the impact reverberating up his arm, and countered with a hook that landed squarely on the man's jaw. The man staggered, but didn't fall.
	"Kill. Kill. Kill." the voice whispered in his ear. Connor flinched.
	He pressed forward, throwing a barrage of strikes, each one more calculated than the last.
	The man in uniform grinned, his black-veined eyes glinting in the flashlight's beam. He ducked under a punch and landed a knee to Connor's stomach, sending him skidding back a few steps.
	Pain bloomed in Connor's gut, but he straightened quickly, his expression hardening. He was stronger. He grinned.
	"LISTEN AND OBEY!" the man shouted.
	Connor froze for a split second, before regaining his focus. "FUCK YOU!" he screamed back.
	The uniformed man lunged again, but this time Connor sidestepped and landed a devastating elbow to the man's ribs.
	The crack of bone was audible. The man grunted in pain, but Connor didn't let up. He grabbed the man's arm, twisted it, and drove his knee into the side of the man's leg. The sound of it snapping filled the room.
	The man collapsed to one knee, snarling in agony. Connor followed with a brutal kick to the head, sending him sprawling onto the floor.
	Connor planted a boot on the man's chest, pinning him. His hand darted down, grabbing the man by the throat. His voice was low and dangerous as he growled, "Who are you people, and what did you do to me?!"
	The uniformed man stared back, defiantly. "Fuck you, traitor."
	Connor growled, and tightened his grip. "I don't mind killing freaks like you. *WHO ARE YOU?!*"
	The man drew a knife, aiming for Connor's side. Connor grabbed the knife and drove it into the man's throat.
	He gasped, and reached out, before expiring.
	Connor sighed, and stood. He exhaled sharply, and de-formed the balaclava. Turning to the boxes, he waved the flashlight inside. Syringes. Dozens of them. His jaw tightened. He grabbed one, lit a match, and threw it into the box, burning the rest. He went off home.

	The room was dark. Connor's flat was untidy.
	He climbed in through an open window and removed his mask, before sighing and pulling out a drawing board. He crossed off an item on a list, stepped back, and sighed again. He pulled out his phone.
	"Johnny, it's me."
	"Anything?" Johnny asked.
	"No, nothing. Managed to grab whatever he was pushing on 'em, though - some kind of syringe."
	"Probably the steroids Slater was freaking about." Johnny said. "How was the fight?"
	"Not as bad as last time." Connor began. "Only killed one person - he was enhanced, like me - but weaker. I didn't have much of a choice."
	"You had *no* choice. What about the others?"
	"They're hurt, but they'll live. I've, uh... I'm getting better at holding back."
	"That's good."
	"Yeah." Connor nodded. "Also, I took one of the syringes with me."
	"What for?"
	"Well, I figured it'd be good to look into it - once I find someone who can. Either way, no good leaving that shit on the streets."
	"Fair enough. Anyway, I got you a lead."
	"What lead?"
	"Marsh Road, Belson. Warehouse 5-2-59/B. Slater is meeting with these freaks."
	Connor's eyes flashed with anticipation. "I'm on it."

SCENE
	In Belson, Slater and a couple of his goons were meeting two men in military uniforms. Connor was hidden behind a couple of boxes, listening in.
	"You disappoint us, Slater." one of the uniformed men began.
	"Oh yeah? Well you lot are selling 'roids on my streets without my say-so." Slater replied, trying to sound tough.
	"Not steroids - but you wouldn't get it. You've been taking from us." the other man muttered.
	"Any operations on my streets gotta be done with my say-so. Otherwise, it's fair game."
	"I'll show you fair game." the first growled, pulling out a silenced pistol and shooting both goons in the head. He then shot Slater in the abdomen. Connor gasped, giving away his position.
	"Get him!" the first man barked.
	Connor didn't hesitate. He leaped over the boxes, moving with inhuman speed, and grabbed the armed man in a headlock. With a twist of his body, he pivoted, using his momentum to snap the man's neck in one smooth motion. The body crumpled, lifeless.
	The second man reacted quickly, grabbing a crowbar from a nearby crate and swinging it with brutal force. The blow landed squarely on Connor's head, sending him sprawling onto his back. Pain flared in his skull.
	The crowbar hit him again with a sickening crack, but the pain didn't register immediately. His vision blurred for a moment.
	As Connor laid on the ground, he felt his costume shudder and shake. It re-formed into the armoured bodysuit from his flat.
	The man raised the crowbar again, aiming for Connor's face. But his hand shot up, catching the weapon mid-swing. With a sharp kick, Connor sent the man staggering backwards.
	He sprang to his feet in an unnatural way - as though he were a marionette.
	He swung the crowbar in a wide arc, smashing it into the man's face. The impact sent him stumbling, blood pouring from his shattered nose.
	As the man stumbled, Connor felt his muscles shudder and tremble.
	Before he could recover, Connor swept the man's legs, sending him into the air. He finished by driving the crowbar into his chest. The steel pierced through with a sickening crunch, pinning the man to the ground. His body jerked once, then went still.
	Connor stood over him, his breath ragged. For a moment, he shuddered, staring at the blood on his hands and the bodies around him.
	"Kill. Kill. Kill." the voice whispered.
	Shaking it off, he turned to Slater, who was slumped against a crate, groaning in pain.
	"Why are you meeting with these freaks, Slater?" Connor asked, preparing to interrogate him. Thankfully, Slater was a coward in pain, so he spilled.
	"Th-they've been selling 'roids, trying to shack up with the Patriots - we've got nothing to do with them, I swear!" he relayed, panicking.
	"They're with the Patriots? I thought your lot were with them."
	"Stupid git..." Slater spats. "We split from those losers years ago. But you golliwog-lovers think we're all the same--aghh!"
	Connor whacked Slater.
	"Where can I find them?" he snarled.
	"I don't know... I don't... I need..." Slater hyperventilated, before passing out.
	Connor sighed, and looked up.
	He whispered "Why am I going to do this?" before pulling out his phone.
	"999, what emergency service do you require?" the phone operator said calmly.
	"Hello, yes, I need an ambulance, I've had an accident and I'm bleeding out. I'm at Marsh Road, Belson, Warehouse 5-2-59/B. Goodbye." He said in an imitation of Slater's voice, before hanging up.
	He looked at himself in a metal sheet. He observed his new costume - it looked like an edgy superhero getup. But it was tough - tougher than kevlar. And it completely masked his appearance - not even a close friend would recognise him.
	"Okay..." he smirked. "This will come in handy."
	Then, he felt a final shudder - liquid exited the palm of his hand and hardened into a knife.
	He held the knife up, and smirked again.
	"But not as much as that."
	
	Connor then walked outside. He took a deep breath, but before he could exhale...
	FF-WHACK!
	He felt his leg buckle. He looked down and saw a bullet had torn right through his thigh and landed in the ground below.
	In less than a microsecond, he realised the direction of fire, and darted for cover behind a dumpster. A second bullet narrowly missed him, grazing his arm.
	Then, the pain hit. He clutched the entry and exit wounds, and his eyes flashed bright red for a second, before returning to their normal steel-grey.
	He stuck his head out, but immediately ducked as a bullet whizzed overhead. He spotted a crack in the wall he was covered by, and peeked through that.
	A sniper, perched on a rooftop above him. He shuddered.
	No choice.
	He leaped out from cover, sprinting in a zig-zag pattern. The sniper's bullets whizzed past him, and one found its mark in his gut. It carved through his intestines, and tore out of his back, taking chunks of flesh with it.
	Undaunted, he sprinted on, the thrill of the fight masking his agony. He dived through a ground-floor window into the building the sniper had perched on.
	"Chyort voz'mi..." he heard him mutter. He sprinted up the stairs, the sniper sprinted down. They met in a stairwell.
	The sniper drew a sawn-off shotgun, and unloaded both barrels into Connor's chest.
	He flew backwards, crashing into the wall behind him. He struggled to his feet, his eyes flashing red again.
	"Bozhe moy!" the sniper shuddered, scrambling to reload.
	Before he could, Connor grabbed the gun, and effortlessly yanked it from his hands. His own fists morphed into claws, and he lifted the shooter up by the throat.
	"WHO ARE YOU PEOPLE?!" he screamed. "WHAT DID YOU DO TO ME?!"
	"US?! YOU NAZI BASTARD!" the sniper spat back.
	"ME?! I'm not the one selling freaky steroids to Slater's lot!"
	He tightened his grip.
	"Tell me who you people are, *right now* - or I'll pop your head like a grape."
	The sniper scowled. "You need to do better than that. I'll gladly die before I give up my secrets to a fascist pig." he sputtered.
	Connor snarled, then released his grip. Dropping his bravado, the sniper choked and spat, catching his breath. He pulled off his balaclava, revealing black receding hair and a thick beard.
	"The fuck are you talking about? You're the ones who are working with these cunts!"
	"Ty chto?!" he pulled his head back incredulously. "Wait a minute... you're *not* with those freaks?"
	"I just killed three of them this evening, you prick!" Connor growled in his face. "And I'll happily kill a fourth, if you don't start talking!"
	Realisation dawned on his face. He grinned, and brushed himself off, before offering his hand out.
	"Ivan Sokolov. KGB - or what's left of it. Apologies for the... introduction, but we thought you were with them."
	Connor tilted his head, not taking the hand. He un-morphed his mask to reveal his face. "Why would I be with them? They shot me in the head and turned me into a monster!"
	"Da, and we thought they'd got your soul, too." Ivan nodded. "We know this... cabal, they have brainwashing technology. But if you're fighting them, it clearly didn't work on you. By now, they would have said your keywords."
	Connor shuddered. "They... They said 'Listen and Obey' to me a couple times. It makes me pause, but nothing more."
	Ivan stroked his beard. "Then their conditioning didn't take too deep a root. Good, very good. How's your leg? And your gut?"
	"I'll live." Connor chuckled grimly. "Shoot me again, and you're dead."
	Ivan laughed. "Fair enough, tovarishch."
	He paused.
	"You want to take the fight to these bastards?"
	Connor nodded.
	"Then follow me."
	"To where?"
	"I have mission for you." Ivan began. "You and me. We arrive at destination - warehouse occupied by these freaks. You go in, loud - kill them while I sneak in, then we take the stuff they have."
	"What stuff do they have?" Connor asked, raising an eyebrow.
	"Don't know - but secret, military shit." Ivan replied.
	"How far's the drive?"
	"2 hours. Why?"
	"Because some Russian bastard shot me a bunch, and I need some time to regenerate." Connor laughed.
	Ivan chuckled, and the pair headed downstairs.
	Connor stood there in the alleyway for a moment, deep in thought.
	"The KGB..." he muttered. "What the fuck..."

	A man in a creased trench coat sat at his desk, rubbing tired eyes beneath short, receding brown hair. He had a detective's badge, a beer belly under his shirt, and stubble from too many late nights.
	A young south-asian woman in a PC uniform approached his desk.
	"DI Naismith, sir? PC Nina Chowdhury, sir." she said timidly.
	Naismith stood, smiled, and extended his hand. "Pleased to meet you, PC Chowdhury. DI Henry Naismith. How can I help?"
	Nina smiled, and shook his hand. "New case just came in, sir - the Chief Constable himself asked me to deliver it to you."
	"They've got PCs doing admin work now? Bloody budget cuts." Naismith chuckled.
	"Tell me about it, sir." Nina replied, still smiling, placing the files on Naismith's desk. "Sir." she nodded respectfully as she left.
	Naismith read through the files - the words "Vigilante Killings", "Redbridge Gangs", "Unnatural strength and stamina", and "Experimental steroid usage?" were visible. He sighed. 

	An hour later, Connor overlooked a group of Super-Agents - each one with the tell-tale black-veined eye sockets of genetically enhanced super-soldiers.
	He descended, moving faster than any human could follow, dropping down into the middle of the group with a sickening crack of bones.
	The fight was brutal and fast. Connor tore through them, his punches and kicks landing with devastating precision. He didn't hold back - they weren't people, not anymore. They were weapons, and they needed to be neutralised.
	"Kill! Kill! Kill!" the voice demanded. Connor grinned - for once, he could agree with it.
	His vision blurred as he took a punch. His legs felt heavy, the pain in his hamstring felt sharp - he was strong, but not invulnerable.
	One Agent lunged at him, a blade flashing in the moonlight. Connor caught his wrist, twisted, and snapped the man's arm in a single motion.
	Another Agent charged from the side, but he anticipated the attack, sidestepping and landing a crushing blow to the back of the man's skull.
	As Connor finished off the last Agent, police arrived on the scene. Bullets tore through the air, grazing Connor's chest.
	Connor sprinted away, but Naismith aimed his pistol. "ARMED POLICE!" he shouted, and his shot hit its mark - Connor's hamstring.
	The bullet ripped through Connor's flesh.
	The pain was sharp, but Connor kept running. His legs ached, but they still carried him forward. He stumbled slightly, but didn't stop.
	Naismith watched in disbelief. He muttered under his breath, his eyes wide in stunned confusion. "How the hell...?"
	Connor sprinted down the alley, but before he could fully escape, a motorcycle cop zipped into view. The officer tased him from behind, sending a shock of agony through his body.
	Connor recoiled, gasping, the pain sharper than the bullet wound. But his instincts kicked in, and he fought through it, turning just in time to kick the officer in the face. The officer's helmet shattered, and he slumped unconscious.
	"Kill! Kill! Kill!"
	Connor shook his head, banishing the voice. "Not humans." he muttered.
	He grabbed the officer's motorbike, revved the engine, and sped off into the night, weaving through traffic with reckless abandon. The chase was on, but Connor knew how to lose them. He sped toward the pier, and with one final burst of energy, drove straight off the edge.
	The cold water swallowed him whole. He swam through the murky depths, his body already healing the minor injuries.
	Within moments, he surfaced, gasping for air, and quietly made his way back to shore.

	Connor arrived at his apartment, soaking wet but otherwise unharmed. As he entered, he saw Sparky sitting by the window, panting, his fur ruffled.
	"Rough night." Connor commented. "How did yours go?"
	"Good!" Sparky replied, tail wagging. "Found a place where a bunch of bad men were gathering. Heard one of them say "They'll be at the hog and hounds tomorrow at 10" - I don't know what that means but it sounded important."
	"Hog and Hounds..." Connor said. "That pub was being extorted by Slater's men last I heard. Johnny says that now Slater's in prison, his gang is looking to rejoin the Patriots."
	"Does that mean we're going to fight?" Sparky asked, smiling devilishly.
	"Not we. Me." Connor said firmly, taking out a bag with pills in it. "I need you out tomorrow night patrolling. Johnny says there's been an increase in men spiking girl's drinks - using these pills. Get a good smell on them."
	Sparky sniffed the bag, and nodded.
	"I need you to patrol the clubs and, if you see any men with these pills, maul 'em."
	"Even better." Sparky replied, a glint in his eye. "And you'll be at this pub of theirs?"
	"That's right." Connor said. "Last thing we need is Slater's lot making a comeback with Patriot backing - or, heaven forbid, getting their hands on those syringes."
	Connor looked outside, lost in thought.
	"The cops were on my tail faster than usual - they almost caught me this time. I think they're getting lairy."
	"Is that bad?" asked Sparky.
	"If they find out who we really are, very." Connor said matter-of-factly. "I'm seeing Ivan next week - I'll see if he can pull some strings."
	Connor's vision blurred for a second, the pain from his hamstring and the lingering shock from the taser flooding his mind.

He dropped from the second floor, landing onto the concrete below with a thud. His legs bent slightly with the impact, but he didn't flinch. He was getting better at ignoring what would kill a human.

	He strode into the pub, and immediately, a group of rough men pulled out knives, clubs, and a few rusty pipes.
	The first man swung a knife toward him. Connor dodged, stepping into the strike and driving his fist into the man's gut, winding him. The man stumbled back, gasping for air. Connor didn't wait for him to recover; he swung a brutal right hook to another man's chin, sending him crashing to the ground.

	By the time he reached the tenth, he heard the unmistakable sound of a shotgun being cocked.
	Chk-chk! BANG!
	The pellets tore into Connor's abdomen. He staggered back, pain flashing through him as his body slammed into the wall behind.
	He gritted his teeth, pushing through the pain as he slowly rose to his feet. But before he could fully recover, he heard another BANG!
	This time, the shotgun was aimed directly at his face. The blast ripped through his features, and Connor's seemingly lifeless body crumpled to the ground.
	The gunman smirked. He turned to his remaining men, barking orders.
	"Clean up this fucking mess! Last thing we need is looking like a bunch of pussies when the Patriots get here!"
	One of the goons, grinning, stared at Connor's body. "Would a bunch of pussies kill that little wanker?"
	Another voice chimed in, panicked. "Fuck that - we need to get out. The cops will have been called by now - you fucking shot him!"
	"It was self-defence." the gunman growled. "The little faggot tried to start shit, and we retaliated."
	He paused, glancing down at Connor's motionless form. "You know, this is the wanker that's been giving the Patriots trouble. But you know what, cunt? You don't look so tough."
	Just as he leant in to gloat, Connor's eyes snapped open, glowing with an unnatural red hue.
	"KILL. KILL. KILL." the voice screamed.
	Without warning, Connor's hand shot out, grabbing the gunman by the throat with terrifying strength. The man choked, his eyes bulging in panic as Connor effortlessly slammed him to the ground.
	The gun clattered away, but Connor grabbed it with one hand, holding it by the barrel, and began to beat the gunman's head into the floor with savage force. The sickening sound of bone cracking filled the room as the man's skull collapsed.
	The other men, now trembling in fear, screamed and scattered like rats, rushing out of the pub as fast as they could.
	Connor's breath came in heavy, ragged gasps as he stood over the remains of the gunman.
	His hand was slick with blood, and his heart was still pounding with adrenaline. His eyes slowly faded from glowing red to their normal steel-grey colour as he regained some semblance of control.
	He looked down at his hands, now covered in the man's blood. His body shook involuntarily, and he stumbled back, retching violently. The bile rose in his throat, and he vomited on the floor.
	He took a deep breath, steadying himself. Reaching up, he morphed his mask back into place, covering his face, and then stood, a little unsteady, before walking to the bar.
	He poured himself a pint, his hands still trembling slightly. He wiped the blood from his palms with a rag, his eyes briefly flickering toward the lifeless body of the gunman.
	"I had to. I had to do it. But..."
	His hands trembled as the man's screams echoed in his mind. Was there no other way?
	He shook his head, trying to banish the thoughts. But they stuck, clinging to him like a second skin.
	"Am I becoming one of them?"
	Connor shuddered, taking a long drink from his pint. The bitter taste did little to wash away the gnawing sense of guilt.
	Suddenly, the door crashed open. Police officers stormed into the pub, assault rifles raised.
	"For fuck's sake!" Connor growled under his breath, tossing the pint aside and diving out the window in one fluid motion. Glass shattered as he leaped, just as bullets tore through the air, filling the space he had just occupied.
	He landed in the alleyway below, but the officers were quick to follow. Connor sprinted, instinctively grabbing onto a nearby wall. His fingers latched onto it, and for a moment, he just stood there, eyes wide in realization.
	He looked down at his gloved hands. The suit's gloves had morphed into a special adhesive, allowing him to scale the wall with ease. Without a second thought, he began to climb, moving up the building like a spider.
	As he reached the top, he took one last glance down, ensuring no one was close. He sprinted across the rooftop, disappearing into the night.

	Thanking his suit, he returned to the flat, went into the bathroom, approached the mirror, and un-morphed his mask.
	His face was torn and bruised, but healing. The shotgun pellets grazed right off of his skull, only tearing his flesh - and he knew his flesh healed quickly. He made himself a high-calorie protein shake to stimulate his healing, and fell asleep on his bed.
	As he slept, he saw visions again. Him beating the man's head in - but again, it felt like he was merely observing it.
	He was filled with animalistic rage... like some kind of berserker. He woke up in a cold sweat. He headed to the bathroom, ran the cold tap, washed his face, and looked in the mirror. Only light bruising and grazing of the skin remained. He smiled slightly, and ran himself a bath.
	As he has his bath, he heard Sparky coming in through the window.

Hell, as I learned tonight, even shotgun blasts to the face can't kill us. Even having a gun is no longer justification for us to kill them - because we don't have to kill them to stop them from being a threat. But the Agents, the men like us..." Connor's face hardened. They're super-human, and can't be contained the way normal humans can. Normal people, even bad normal people, can be knocked out and locked away and no longer be a threat to anyone. The freaks with the black eyesockets? There's no way to stop them from being a threat, save killing 'em."

	"Good boy." he said gently. The old dog raised his head, smiled, and went back to sleep. Naismith looked down at his alarm clock. It was 5AM.
	He headed downstairs and made himself a coffee. He was wearing a dirty white T-shirt and boxers.
	He drank his coffee, then headed into the bathroom. He noticed his stubble was threatening to grow into a full beard. He sighed, sprays some deodorant, and got dressed. He gave his dog a stroke.
	"I'll be back later, Max. I'll take you out for a walk, yeah?"
	The dog smiled softly. Naismith headed to the kitchen, checked the dog door was still working, and filled Max's bowls with dog food and water. He sighed, aching somewhat, and headed outside to his car. He entered the car, sighed again, and closed his eyes.
	With that, Connor leant forward, revealing himself to have been sitting in the back seat.
	"Morning, Inspector." he said in a deep, gravelly voice.
	Naismith reached for his gun, but Connor drew his own, and pushed it into Naismith's temple.
	"That would be very foolish." he growled. Naismith nodded and released, holding both hands in the air.
	"Gun. Now." Connor barked. "Any sudden moves, your brains'll paint the window."
	Naismith nodded. "Okay. Okay. I'm doing as you say."
	He pulled out his handgun, and passed it to Connor. Satisfied, Connor put both guns down.
	"There." he said. "Now we can talk like grown ups. Never liked guns anyway."
	"What, not visceral enough a method of killing for your tastes?" Naismith snarled in an accusatory tone.
	"Hm? No, I just don't want you to shoot me in the face again. Besides, it's the opposite." Connor chuckled grimly. "With your hands, it's much easier to subdue someone without killing them. You can be deliberate. Guns... It's hard to shoot someone non-lethally. The way I see it, if I use my hands, I make sure everyone I kill, I did it on purpose. My conscience can be clean."
	"A clean conscience?! Did you see the man you butchered at the Hog and Hounds? We had to scoop his brains back in with a spoon!" Naismith replied indignantly.
	"After he shot me in the face with a shotgun. Tell me, Inspector - would you be in control of yourself after that?"
	"I wouldn't be anything, I'd be dead - because I'm not some freak of nature!"
	"Oh, I'm a freak all right - but nature had nothing to do with this." Connor chuckled. "Someone else did. And to find out who... I need your help."
	"What?!" Naismith laughed incredulously. "That's a new one. Never had a criminal come to me for help."
	"Naismith." Connor interrupted. "I read your file. Seems you're well known as the office rat - you've arrested 5 other officers in your career. And, you made it to Detective Inspector, which means you're clever. So, a clever man with morals. If you can't see there's something bigger going on, no one can."
	"I see two things - right and wrong. The law." Naismith inhaled. "And criminality. And I know which side I'm on."
	"Oh, I couldn't agree more - there's right and wrong. Black and white. Where you are wrong..." Connor said, his mask hiding his smirk, "Is which side the law's on. The law is the arm of power. And power has a name. ODESSA."
	"What are you talking about?!" Naismith sighed, exasperated.
	"No. If I tell you, you won't believe me. You need to see it for yourself." Connor replied. "I'm going to attack somewhere tonight. I won't tell you where, so you don't crash the party too early - but it's in Marsh Road. Have yourself and your people on standby, and listen out for sounds of a fight. It'll begin at 10pm. Try not to shoot me in the face again."
	Naismith shook his head. "Why would you tell me that?"
	"So you can get there on time. And see the truth first-hand." Connor nodded.
	Naismith thought for a moment. "It sounds like I'm doing your dirty work for you."
	"No. You're responding to a threat from a serial killer, right?" Connor interjected. "A known, wanted criminal told you where he plans to strike. So, you have a duty to arrive on the scene, no? Besides, you kind of owe me for trying to kill me last week."
	Naismith sighed. "...fine. I'll be there."
	Connor breathed a sigh of relief. He unloaded Naismith's gun, placed it on the back seats, and exited the car. 
	Naismith rested his head on the steering wheel, and sighed again.
	"What the fuck am I getting myself into?" he whispered aloud.

Tipping off Naismith

SCENE
	Naismith and Nina sat in the car, parked up in Marsh Road. Nina was sipping a coffee cup, as Naismith looked out the window, deep in thought.
	"So..." she began. "Do you want to tell me why we're here, sir?"
	"I got a tip off from a CHIS I've been working with." Naismith replied. "Supposedly, the Werewolf plans to hit somewhere here tonight. We're always arriving late to these, so..." he paused. "If we get there as it happens, maybe we can catch the bastard."
	Nina smiled and nodded. "It's a shame we couldn't get armed backup."
	"Yeah... budget cuts." Naismith sighed. "Dorsey's putting all the pressure on us to catch this guy, but he's not giving us anything to work with..."
	"Between you and me, sir... I think Dorsey was appointed Chief Constable because he knows how to please the politicians, rather than any actual competance." She anxiously awaited Naismith's reaction, scared of seeming unprofessional. Naismith chuckled, causing her to relax.
	"You got that right..." he replied. "To tell you the truth, I think he's a real--" he said, before being cut off by a cracking sound in the distance.
	"Gunshots." he snapped into action. He started the car and drove toward the source. Nina put on her bulletproof vest.
	"Control, this is Oscar Charlie 5-2." she said to her radio. "Gunshots heard on Marsh Road. Investigating now."
	"Received, 5-2. Backup ETA is 19 minutes. Proceed with extreme caution, disengage if needed."
	They arrived at the warehouse where the showdown was taking place, and jumped out of the car, pistols drawn.
	"ARMED POLICE!" they both shouted, only to put their guns down in horror.
	The scene that unfolded before them was beyond comprehension. They saw Connor, suited up and battling a man... no. Not a man. A giant of a man, easily 8 foot tall, and built like an ogre. Every swing of his fists sent shockwaves through the air.
	Connor moved like water, agile and precise. He ducked under a punch, tearing a hole through the wall behind him. His breath was steady, but there was a bestial cunning in his eyes as he calculated his next move.
	Nina stared in horror, as Naismith opened fire on the Giant. The bullets hit his chest, but to no effect.
	The Giant barely flinched. Naismith cursed under his breath and switched tactics, trying to find a weak spot.
	"C-c-control, v-vigilante suspect currently engaged in melee with--with..." Nina stammered into the radio.
	"Repeat, 5-2, what is the situation?"
	"A-a Giant! There's a fuckin' Giant in here!" Nina shrieked back.
	Out of nowhere, a second figure leaped from the shadows - Sparky, clad in his own costume. He landed on the Giant's shoulder, teeth sinking into his flesh with a sickening squelch. The Giant howled in pain, momentarily distracted.
	"Repeat, 5-2. Did you say 'Giant'?" Control asked incredulously.
	Nina ignored it, and shot the Giant. The bullet glanced off, and buried into a wall.
	With that, a loud boom filled the warehouse. From above, a figure emerged from the shadows - another soldier, this one dressed in full kevlar and crouching in the rafters like a spider in its web. Ivan. He steadied his rifle, and without hesitation, fired.
	The bullet flew through the air with deadly precision, and with a thwack, it slammed into the giant's chest. It punched through the thick muscle and bone as if they were made of paper, sending the Giant stumbling back with a gargled roar of agony.
	"Khoroshaya devochka, Isabella." he whispered, blowing his rifle a kiss.
	Connor wasted no time. He charged.
	With a savage, calculated strike, he delivered a devastating blow to the Giant's knee, causing the massive creature to topple like a felled tree.
	He didn't stop there. He pressed his advantage, stepping over the fallen giant and delivering a bone-shattering stomp to its head. The force of the impact was enough to make the warehouse floor tremble. The Giant's skull caved in with a sickening crunch, and blood splattered across the cold concrete.
	For a moment, the giant twitched - like a butchered pig in its final moments - but then all went still.
	Connor stood over the massive corpse, his chest heaving with labored breaths, his eyes glowing faintly red in the dim light. He surveyed the room.
	Naismith ran to Nina's side - her face was pale and her hands trembled. Her gun was pointed at Connor.
	"Armed... Armed police... Sto-stop right th-there..." she said, shaking and stuttering. "Y-you do not have to say anything, b-but it may harm your defence if... if..."
	Naismith gently placed his hand on her shoulder.
	"Nina. It's okay. Put down the gun." he whispered comfortingly. She looked at him, and holstered her gun, a single tear of fear running down her cheek.
	"What... What was that?!" he asked, facing Connor.
	Connor took a deep breath.
	"That was their latest attempt at making a living weapon." he said, kicking his boot out to shake off the brains of the Giant. He sauntered over to a desk, where a man in labcoat's body laid. He grabbed a small device from the corpse. Sparky trotted towards him.
	Ivan jumped down. "We got reports that they had deployed such a monster to the city." he said grimly. "If this won't convince you something horrible is brewing, nothing will."
	"What... What are we supposed to do now?" Naismith asked. Nina looked at him, shocked.
	"Sir... Did... Did you know?" she trembled.
	"No! Nina, I swear... I only knew the Werewolf would be here. He told me he would 'show me the truth' - I didn't think it would be this."
	Nina paused, then nodded silently.
	"*We* don't do anything." Connor replied in answer to Naismith's question. "You call it in, and reveal what you saw here. Then, have this body analysed - I'm sure you'll find some interesting facts about its biology."
	Naismith nodded.
	Connor looked over at Nina. She was... familiar. Then, he saw a brief flash - Yasmin, his ex. He shuddered.
	Nina grabbed her radio, nodded at Naismith, and spoke into it. "Control, this is Oscar Charlie 5-2. Situation under control, unarmed clear to approach. Location is Marsh Road, unit 7-8-24/D. One body - abnormal. Assailant has fled the scene. Request immediate deployment of forensic investigators."
	"Received, 5-2. FI's en route, ETA 24 minutes." the radio replied.

	Connor, Sparky, and Ivan met back up at Connor's flat. Connor revealed the device he secured - a hard-drive. Ivan plugged it into a rugged laptop he brought, and began to study the data. As he scrolled through, his face turned pale - well, paler. The black veins on his eyesockets, that constant reminder of Connor's salvation, darkened even more. He turned to face his comrades.
	"Bad. Very, very bad." he said.
	"What? What is it?" Connor asked, wide-eyed.
	Ivan showed him a document. It included reports on serum production, ETAs for building a super-agent army... and a name. A name of a company.
	"Morland... Morland is connected to ODESSA."
	Connor grew pale too. "Chloe..." he gasped.
	"Who?" Ivan asked.
	"No, no-one. She's not..." Connor began, but sighed.
	"She's a friend of mine. She works at Morland - she's on university placement there. She's been assigned to my case for some reason."
	"Could she be involved?" Ivan asked, but Connor immediately shook his head.
	"No. Absolutely not. For one thing, given ODESSA's ideology, there's no way they'd recruit a disabled woman. Second, she's just not like that."
	"Okay... But you said she's in university, da? Why would she be assigned to this case?"
	"I don't know... But ODESSA have to know who I am. And thus, we have to assume they know who she is." Connor shuddered, aghast at the idea that he'd drawn Chloe into this. "Maybe they had her assigned to try and sabotage things? I mean, if it came out that the Werewolf's friend was in on the investigation, they could discredit the whole thing."
	"Maybe. Or maybe they're keeping her involved as leverage against you." Ivan said grimly.
	"I won't allow that." Connor replied, his voice as cold as ice. "I will burn their entire cabal to the ground if they even touch a hair on her head."
	Ivan smirked. "Well, burning their whole cabal to the ground was already the plan, da?"
	Connor smirked back. "Well, yes. But if they take things that far, I'm not fighting them in the shadows anymore. What will they do, arrest me? I'd like to see them try."
	"Be careful." Ivan said, concerned. "The moment you remove any restrictions in your mission, is the moment you surrender to your basest instincts."
	"Instincts are what we are." Sparky added. "If they come for our pack, we'll destroy them. *Destroy.*" he growled.
	Ivan looked down, unable to understand. "What did he say?"
	"He said..." Connor hesitated. "He said if they come for our pack, we'll destroy them."
	Ivan chuckled. "Well, I can't blame a wolf for following his gut. And I'm not saying don't fight them. I'm saying... Don't forget, you're still a man."
	Connor paused for thought. He was so far-removed from humanity... could he still count himself among them?
	"Hey..." Ivan began. "We've made a huge dent today. Things'll be pretty quiet for a while - and Christmas is coming up. Maybe you should take some time off? You don't need to be the hero every day." he said, with a somewhat fatherly concern.
	"Good thinking..." Connor replied, nodding.

Killing the Giant
______________________________
SCENE
	In the bowels of Morland Genetics, the Autopsy Suite's lights shone eerily. In the centre, a table with the Giant's headless corpse strewn over it. A man wearing white scrubs and a surgical mask approached, along with Chloe, who was dressed the same.
	"Okay, so, I'm guessing you've never done an autopsy before?" the man began, taking out his tools.
	"Uh, no... this is my first." said Chloe, uncomfortable.
	"Well, not to make light of it, but they're not normally this big." the man chuckled. Above the mask, Chloe's eyes creased - she was smirking. Satisfied he'd relaxed her a little, the man pulled out a circular saw.
	"So, I'll use this to open up his chest cavity, and then we'll use the spreader to open up the ribcage. From there, we can begin extracting his internal organs, and take a look at them."
	"Mm-hm." Chloe responded, trembling at the thought.
	The man smiled, and began to use the saw. Despite the size and high quality, the saw took much, much longer than usual to cut through.
	"Hmph... Get.. In... There!" the man said, finally cutting in. "Whew, okay, so, initial findings?" he looked up at Chloe.
	"Well..." Chloe said, clicking her pen to begin writing on her notepad, "His skin and muscles are clearly much tougher than normal humans. The fact that the saw is struggling to cut through his chest means his tissue density is far beyond normal levels. It's like trying to slice through a reinforced steel plate with a butter knife. The muscle fibres are denser, almost like they've been artificially toughened."
	"Very good." the man nodded. "External injuries?"
	"You mean aside from the mulch pile where his head should be?" Chloe asked, making the man chuckle. "I can see a bullet wound... there." she pointed to a hole in the chest. "According to officer statements, this was caused by a high-caliber bullet fired by a sniper rifle. Police ballistic analysis reported that the bulled had a carbon plating on the tip, which made it much sharper - so the assailants knew that this man needed a lot to take down."
	"Any other, non-fatal injuries?" the man asked, waiting to see Chloe's reaction.
	"Hmm... there!" she said, pointing to his leg and abdomen. "Small wounds, likely caused by the officer's attempts to shoot him. The bullets made an impact, causing friction burns and bruising, but did not pierce the skin. And... teeth marks on the shoulder, consistent with the description of the 'werewolf' present. But what stands out to me is the depth of those marks. They're not just punctures; they're almost like the bite force was so extreme that it crushed through the muscle fibres and into the bone. How could something bite harder than our saws? Anyway..." she banished the thought.
	"Very good!" the man said, satisfied. "Okay, let's open him up. Spreader?"
	Chloe handed him the tool, and the man began to spread the ribcage open. He strained under the pressure of using the tool, not expecting it to be so difficult. Eventually, the giant's chest opened with a sickening crunch.
	"Right, now, before I start cutting about willy-nilly, any thoughs about his chest cavity?" the man asked. Chloe leant over to look inside, and gasped audibly.
	"That's... two hearts? Three lungs? And... Four kidneys?! No... those two aren't kidneys. They're adrenal glands, swollen beyond belief." she said, shocked.
	"Wait, adrenal glands? Hang on... You're right." the man tilted his head. "Whatever this thing is, it's had a lot of work done."
	Chloe shuddered, writing down this news. The man began extracting the giant's organs, one-by-one, and placing them in jars for later study. He also cut open the giant's leg, and took a sample of muscle tissue and bone marrow. Once finished, he closed the man back up, and breathed a sigh of relief.
	"Final thoughts?" he asks.
	"You'd think the extra organs would be the biggest one..." Chloe said unsurely. "But I think those adrenal glands could be just as important. The only reason they'd be that big on purpose would be if they're creating more than just adrenaline."
	She thought deeply.
	The man smiled, impressed. "Bet you didn't think your uni placement would be like this, eh?"
	Chloe chuckled. "I'm just glad the Christmas holidays are coming up."
	The man laughed. "Okay, we're all done. Let's get him sealed back up, and you have the joy of dissecting those glands."
	"Yay." Chloe cheered sarcastically, and they hauled the Giant into the freezer. Even with lifting aids and several organs removed, he was incredibly heavy.
	The two breathed out in relief, and left the autopsy room.

Sonic Agony

SCENE
	Naismith stood outside a house door. He sighed, braces himself, and rang the doorbell.
	After a few seconds passed, Ella answered the door.

	"Hi, Miss Branning? DI Naismith." he replied, showing his badge. "May I come in, ma'am?"

And I kept getting the same-old "We are working tirelessly to resolve your case." bullshit! I'm sorry, but what else was I supposed to do?"
	"Wait, hold on..." Naismith rubbed his eyes. "Are you saying that the police knew about Zack's connection to these freaks, and did nothing?"
	"I told them everything. Sent over all of Zack's weird files on them. There was one detective who listened, but she just disappeared halfway through the case. Some new bloke took over and didn't seem to know anything." she explained.

SCENE
	It was near midnight. Connor was running across rooftops and jumping over alleyways, his superhuman senses keeping him keenly aware of the city below.

	Normally, when in costume, he made his voice far, far deeper - an intimidation tactic, and a disguise all the same. But here, his voice was soft, unmodified.
	"I..." the girl began. "Sure. Free country."
	Connor smiled, before remembering she couldn't see his face through the mask.
	He nodded, and sat next to her.
	"So... What's got you up here?" he asked.
	"I'm sat on a rooftop ledge with a bottle of vodka. What do you think?" she replied, before shaking her head. "Sorry, it's just..."
	"It's okay. If someone in pain snapping at a stupid question was enough to phase me, I'd be long dead." Connor chuckled grimly.
	The girl chuckled too. "I... I'm under a lot of stress." she admitted.
	"Wanna tell me why?" Connor asked, silently moving so that if she did jump, he would catch her.
	"I'm a freak." she began, choking back tears.
	"I regrew a hand once." Connor replied. "Like a lizard. Also, I inhaled a whole tank of Chlorine and once got shot in the face with a shotgun, and all it did was piss me off."
	He smiled. "My point is, I'm the last man on Earth who can sit in judgement. You can talk to me."
	The girl looked at him, and tilted her head. "I..." she began, "My parents are kicking me out. They're angry because... Because I want to be a girl."
	Connor pulled his head back, surprised. "Oh, you're trans?"
	"Yeah..." the girl replied, looking sad. "I... I know, it's..."
	"Don't worry." he cut in, trying to sound reassuring. "What's your name? Your real name, I mean."
	"I..." she began. "My parents called me--"
	"No, not that one." Connor interjected. "Your *real* name."
	She smiled softly, encouraged by Connor's acceptance. "I call myself Siobhan."
	Connor smiled, and nodded his head. "Pleased to meet you, Siobhan. And can I say, that name is awesome. Great choice. Of course, as you can tell from the accent, I'm biased."
	Siobhan chuckled. "Heh... Thanks."
	"How do you spell it?"
	She smirked. "With a 'bh', don't worry."
	Connor laughed heartily. "Good lass."
	She laughed with him. "I won't ask your name... Kind of defeats the whole point of wearing a mask, eh?"
	Connor snickered. "Where are you staying now?"
	"Nowhere. They, um... only just kicked me out."
	"I know a guy." Connor leant back. "Johnny Crane, boss of the Redbridge Syndicate. How old are you?"
	"18." Siobhan nodded.
	"Still in school?"
	"No, I... I dropped out."
	"Nice one - I dropped out at 17." he chuckled. "Are you any good with tech?"
	"I like computers."
	"Same." Connor smiled. "Well, the Syndiate owns a repair shop in Redbridge. I can get you an apprenticeship there if you like?"
	"I... you'd do that for me?" Siobhan asked, shocked.
	"Sure." he nodded.
	"But... why?" she replied, awestruck.
	"Two things. One, you remind me of myself at your age, and I know what I needed back then. Two, because you're going to do me a favour in return."
	"What favour?"
	"You're going to live. You're not gonna jump off this rooftop, and you're gonna stay alive." Connor replied firmly. "It's absolutely key to my secret superhero mission that there be a computer repair apprentice called Siobhan active in Redbridge."
	Siobhan chuckled. "Well, if it's for your mission..." she picked up her vodka bottle, and poured it away.
	"Damn, I was gonna drink that!" Connor laughed.
	Siobhan smiled - a genuine smile. "Thanks... I, um... I think I'm ready to come down now."
	"Go to the Singing Horse. Say 'the Werewolf' sent you - I'll call ahead. We'll get you somewhere to stay."
	"Thank you..." Siobhan smiled, tears in her eyes.
	"No, thank you." Connor nodded.
	"What for?"

	"Connor!" Johnny answered, smiling. "What can I do for my favourite Werewolf?"
	"There's a girl who'll be turning up to the club tonight - Siobhan. She's been kicked out by her parents. I've told her we can get her a place to stay tonight. She's also pretty tech-savvy - so maybe we could sort something out for her at the repair shop?" Connor explained.
	"Sounds right up our alley. I'll tell Pawel to let her in." Johnny replied, beaming with pride.
	"Call me if there's any issues."
	"You've got it. Hey... Good man." Johnny smiled.
	Connor smiled back. "Thanks. Night, mate."
	He sighed, breathing in the night air. He un-morphed his mask as the rain began to fall.
	He let the water splash over his face, and took a deep breath.

	That same day, Trey was having dinner at his grandparents' house. Trey's uncle and auntie, as well as his two cousins, were present too, though they kept their distance from him. SCENE
	The aftermath of Christmas dinner at the Jefferson household was peaceful, if a little sluggish. The room practically oozed warmth  -  the scent of cinnamon and roast goose still clung to the air. Their dad had retired upstairs for a nap, and their mum had disappeared into the bath nearly an hour ago, likely dozing there too.

	Her phone buzzed softly on the side table. She blinked slowly, and reached for it.
	"Merry Christmas, gorgeous." Charlie had written. "I hope your day's been magical. I've been thinking about you all day. I got you a little something... was wondering if I could see you? Just for a bit. If not, that's okay. I get it xx"
	She smiled, cheeks warming. She tapped out a reply.
	"Merry Christmas! It's been lovely – my family are all in food comas lol. Hope yours has been good too? Xx"
	He replied almost instantly.
	"It's been fine. Quiet. Just wish I had someone around who really gets me, you know? Everyone's so wrapped up in their own little worlds. It would be lovely if you wanted to meet up? Xx"
	Something about the phrasing made Bea pause. She bit her lip, then typed:
	"Where would you want to meet? Xx"
	"Farley Park? Or... you could come to mine? It's warm. I've got mulled wine and an actual fireplace lol xx" he sent.
	Her fingers hovered, hesitant.
	"I can meet at the park for a bit! I can't stay too long though – everyone's asleep but I'll need to be back soon x"
	"Sure." he replied abruptly.
	She stood up quietly and grabbed her coat.
	"Where are you off to?" Tea murmured from beneath the blanket.
	"Just a walk." Bea whispered. "I'll be back soon."
	The streets were cold and slick. The sky was darkening, the stars blurry behind thin clouds. Bea pulled her coat tighter as she reached the park. 
	Charlie stood waiting, hands in his coat pockets, eyes on the ground.
	He looked up and smiled as she approached. "Hey."
	"Hey!" she replied, breath puffing in the cold.
	"I didn't think you'd come." he began. His voice was low. "I thought maybe you'd changed your mind."
	"No, I just didn't want to stay long. Everyone's still up, mostly."
	He pulled a small wrapped box from his coat and handed it to her.
	Bea opened it carefully. Inside was a delicate silver bracelet, etched with a tiny engraving on the inside:
	"I see you."
	She stared at it. "Charlie... this is beautiful."
	He smiled.
	She looked down at the bracelet again. "Thank you. Really."
	He reached forward, brushing her hair behind her ear. "You don't have to say anything. Just being here... it means more than you know."
	She nodded, pushing her face into his hand.
	"I wanted to give you something that reminded you how different you are. How real." he said. "Not like... the people around you."
	She shifted. "Charlie..."
	"I mean, it's nice they're there," he said, too quickly. "But they don't see you. Not like I do. You said yourself you feel like the extra in your own friend group sometimes."
	"I didn't mean it like that," she said, suddenly uncomfortable.
	He studied her for a moment, then reached for her hands. "Come back to mine?"
	She blinked. "What?"
	"Just for a bit." he said quickly. "I've got this bottle of wine I've been saving, and I made mince pies. I thought... maybe we could just have a moment. Something that's ours."
	"I can't, sorry. I should probably head back soon," she said, almost apologetically.
	His expression shifted. The smile disappeared. "Right."
	She frowned. "I'm sorry, I just - "
	"It's fine," he said sharply, pulling his hands away. "It's totally fine. I just thought maybe you'd want to spend time with me. Guess I misread things."
	"Charlie, I--"
	"No, it's okay. Seriously. Don't worry about it." His tone was brittle. "Enjoy your perfect little family night."
	"That's not fair," Bea said, a tremble in her voice.
	He turned away, jaw tight. "You know what? Just forget I asked. I shouldn't have. This was stupid."
	There was a beat of silence, and then, as suddenly as he had snapped, he softened.
	"I'm sorry," he said, running a hand through his hair. "God, I'm such an idiot. You didn't deserve that. I just... I missed you so much today. I guess I let it get to me."
	Bea stood frozen.
	"I'm sorry, Bea. I just thought... I thought we had something. And I thought maybe today, of all days, I'd matter enough to you to get a little of your time. But it's okay. Really."
	He offered a weak smile, eyes sad. "Go home. They'll miss you."
	Bea gulped, a lump in her throat. "Of course you matter to me. It's just... it's Christmas, you know? We see each other every day at uni."
	"You don't have to explain." he said, backing away.
	She didn't reply. She couldn't. Her feet felt stuck to the pavement.
	"Merry Christmas, Bea." he whispered.
	And then he was gone, his footsteps echoing off the wet stones, leaving her standing alone with the bracelet still in her hands.
	She sighed deeply.

The bile rose in his throat, but it was nothing compared to the fire igniting in his chest.
	The Rage simmered when Danes shot him in the face, when Chloe was assaulted, when Hughes gassed him.
	But this... this was different. This place, this depravity, this sickening scene... it ignited a fury stronger than anything he'd ever felt before. It reminded him of Laverty, of what happened to Missy... It was too much.
	"KILL! KILL! KILL!" the voice screamed, drowning out all other noise.
	
	Connor was a living weapon, no question. But here, in this moment - he was more like a WMD. Unstoppable. Unrelenting.
	He was no longer a man - he was a beast, a force of nature, an embodiment of death. Super-Agents and humans alike fell before him, their bodies shredded by his fury. Their screams were swallowed by blood that coated the room, splattering every surface.
	He moved like a whirlwind. His fists crashed into bodies with bone-shattering force, impaling men on his arms. His karate chops were so fierce they sliced through flesh like butter, leaving nothing but mangled remains. A bullet whizzed past him, and he caught it mid-air with the same effortless precision. In a split second, he turned and hurled it back, the projectile tearing through the shooter's chest with lethal accuracy.
	That was what he was now. A creature strong enough to throw bullets as fast as a gun could shoot them. A monster.
	His claws glinted in the dim light as he raised them. He was ready to strike again, but then he saw her. The little girl, trembling, blindfolded and blood-spattered, standing at the centre of his rampage.
	"Kill." the voice continued, uncaring. His blood ran hot, and demanded more blood in turn.
	He froze.
	The rage faltered. His breath came in ragged gasps as he looked at the girl, her body trembling, her fragile form dwarfed by the carnage around her.
	"It's okay..." he panted, his voice softer now. "It's okay. I'm not going to hurt you. The bad men who hurt you are gone."
	The girl, shaking with fear, took a tentative step forward. She was bound at the ankles, her movements hesitant and slow. But she sensed him - sensed the protector in him - and shuffled closer, her arms trembling as she hugged him, burying her face in his chest.
	Connor's heart twisted. For a moment, he was stunned, unsure of what to do. But then, with a deep sigh, he un-morphed his claws, his form shifting back to something more human, more gentle. He wrapped his arms around her, pulling her close, offering comfort in the midst of the chaos.
	"It's okay." he whispered, his voice breaking. "You're safe now."
	The girl sobbed. "Vreau mama mea..." she whispered. Connor sighed sadly, and stroked her hair, calming her. With that, the police came in. Naismith was leading them, and vomited upon entry. The other officers followed suit.
	Connor stood, and barked orders at them. "There are children here. Your duty is to save them, not stop me."
	Naismith looked down at the scene, absorbing the carnage. Dozens of flayed bodies were strewn across the place. The stench of gore made him retch again - but he steeled himself.
	"Officers, first duty is and always has been preservation of life. Locate and secure the remaining children." he rallied the officers out of their stupor.
	"Sir." the officers replied, spreading out.
	Naismith approached Connor and the little girl. "Hey, hey little one. It's okay, you're safe now."
	"Te rog nu ma rani!" she cried, terrified at the clear voice of an older man.
	Connor reassured her. "It's okay." he whispered. "He won't hurt you. He's a friend."
	With that, the little girl stumbled over to Naismith, who picked her up and walked outside with her. He gave Connor a knowing nod of tacit approval, before leaving. Connor leaped with superhuman strength, sticking to the ceiling like a spider. He crawled over to a nearby window, climbed out, and slinked into the night.

	That same night, Chloe was in the lab, along with her supervisor. She was delivering a presentation to Louis Morland, the CEO.
	"Go ahead, Miss Derrington." Morland smiled.

	"Do tell?" Morland tilted his head.
	"See here." Chloe said, showing her presentation. "We've identified a mutated variant of epinephrine, commonly known as adrenaline. But this is different - this is a novel molecular structure, which we've dubbed 'Paradrenaline'."
	"And what does it do?" Morland asked, intrigued.
	"Well, it... It amplifies their physical abilities - Paradrenaline binds more effectively to the adrenergic receptors in the body, particularly the alpha-1 and beta-2 receptors, responsible for increasing heart rate, blood flow, and muscle contraction. The result is a massive enhancement of physical capabilities: regenerative healing, increased reflexes, and a dramatic rise in strength. But--" she paused, "There are side effects."
	Morland leant forward, his gaze intense. "What kind of side effects?"
	"Well..." Chloe cleared her throat. "At low doses, subjects begin to experience neurological symptoms, primarily intense migraines and frequent nosebleeds. These occur due to an overstimulation of the sympathetic nervous system, which causes vasodilation in the brain, increasing pressure and causing the blood vessels to rupture."
	Morland raised an eyebrow but said nothing, so Chloe continued, tapping the screen to show the next slide.
	"At moderate doses, we start seeing seizures. The neurons in the brain become hyper-excitable due to an imbalance in the sodium and potassium ion channels. It's like a short circuit in the nervous system. The more the subject's body is exposed to Paradrenaline, the more severe the disruption becomes."
	Morland winced, his lips curling into a slight smile. "And at high doses?"
	Chloe's voice lowered, growing more serious. "At high doses, the symptoms are catastrophic. Strokes, aneurysms, and cerebral haemorrhages. The vasculature in the brain becomes too fragile, and the heart rate increases to dangerous levels, putting immense strain on the circulatory system."
	Morland watched her intently, considering her words. "But the superhumans, they survive these doses?"
	"Yes." she nodded. "We believe it's due to their enhanced anatomy. Their bodies seem to compensate for the damage. Their regenerative abilities kick in faster than normal, allowing them to recover from the worst effects. But it's still a temporary fix - they can only withstand so much before the damage becomes incapacitating."
	"The potential here..." he murmured. "If only we could mitigate these side effects."
	"I agree, sir." Chloe smiled. "First responders, firefighters, ambulance staff... they could all really benefit from something like this."
	Morland chuckled. "Yes, them too. But I think you'll find defence contractors pay more."

	"I don't care." he said to himself.
	"Yes I do." he admitted.
	Regardless of her, there was a kid involved. He can't let that slide.
	"I'll do it." he finally spoke.
	Nina exhaled in relief, and let him leave.
	Connor went on his phone. He found Yas's number, and unblocked her.
	"Hey. I just spoke with your sister, she's worried about you and the kid. I once promised you I'd always be there for you; and I don't like to break my promises. If you need me, just call. Regardless of everything that happened, you're still someone who meant a lot to me. If you need a friend, I'm here." he wrote.
	He hesitated, and added another line.
	"I've moved place by the way. My new address is 56 Wilbur Ave. If things get too rough and you need a place to stay, just come round."
	He paused. He closed his eyes, and pressed send.

So, that's what I did. I went to his house, and tried to tell him that I wasn't okay with what happened, begging him to see sense. The second time he did it, he was laughing."

I need you to know, I need you to hear... When I look at you, it all melts away. These things you think are flaws, I don't see them that way. They're you. And because they're you, they're amazing too. I know we joke about how tough I am in a fight... but I hope to hell that one day, I can be a tenth as tough as you." he whispered, Chloe hanging on to every word.

She leant forward, and their foreheads rested on each other. They closed their eyes, and remained like this for a while. They embraced.
	"Thank you..." Chloe said at last.
	"No... Thank you. I'm so happy you feel like you can express yourself, even just a little bit more." he replied.
	"We'd better go check on Bea." Chloe said. Connor nodded in agreement - whatever feelings they may have for each other, they could address those later. Bea needed them right now. They went back inside, and the group formed a hug around Bea.
