	"You're right about that, bratan." Ivan replied, his voice betraying his concern. "A squad of Super-Agents was just spotted heading from a garage in Belson towards Redbridge. Sparky's... well, he's a little tied up at the moment."
	As Ivan said this, he looked over. Sparky bit a head off, and howled. "I can do this all night!"
	"You'd best follow them and see what they're up to." Ivan chuckled.
	"On it." Connor replied, like a soldier on mission.

	Back in Redbridge, the bus suddenly came to a stop.
	"The hell?" Trey tilted his head.
	"Roadworks, maybe?" Missy suggested. That idea was dashed by the sound of a gunshot.
	"FUCK!" the group practically yelped in unison. The bus driver slumped down, dead.
	Screams tore into the air, and a trio of Super-Agents stormed in.
	They trained their guns on the gang, and grinned maliciously.
	"All of you." the leader barked. "You're coming with us."
	The passangers of the bus complied, walking timidly out from the bus.
	"Come on..." Missy whispered, too quiet for anyone else to hear. "Save us..."
	With that, the leader ordered the passengers to their knees.
	"Now!" he began. "I'm not gonna lie to you. You're all in some deep, deep trouble."
	"Let us go!" Trey shouted. An Agent grabbed him by the throat.
	"Not your time to speak, monkey-boy." he snarled. Trey looked him in the eye defiantly.
	"Down!" the leader snapped. The Agent huffed, and released his grip.
	"Now then..." he continued. "You've all heard of this 'Werewolf' fella?"
	Silence.
	"No? Maybe you will by the night's end. See, you should all rejoice - even the mulattos, cripples, and freaks among you." he said, faux-magnanimously gesturing to the gang in particular - hardly the picture of Aryan purity - and grinned. "You have all been spared the hangman's noose, by our great and gracious Captain. Instead, you will all suffer... a beating."
	He chuckled. "Start with him."
	Immediately, the Agents pounced on Trey, and savagely beat him. Ever defiant, he fought back, digging his thumbs into one Agent's eye. The Agent replied by slamming Trey's head against the ground, concussing him.
	"Trey! No!" the others begged.
	Missy stood, and tried to grab one. "Leave him alone, you're killing him!"
	The Agent replied by throwing her in the air. She landed on her back, and spluttered.
	"Her next! The half-caste wench." the leader snarled, pointing at Bea. She closed her eyes. Chloe jumped in front of her.
	"LEAVE US ALONE!" she roared. The Agents laughed.

	With that, a bestial snarling noise filled the air.
	"*+GET. AWAY. NOW.+*" Connor barked. His visor glowed a bright red, and his suit morphed claws and spikes throughout his armour. His nickname had always been the Werewolf - but now, he looked the part, too.
	"Finally." the leader grinned. "Welcome back, traitor!"
	Connor stood still, and then he was a blur. He pounced on the leader, and delivered a haymaker that send him skidding on the tarmac.
	The other agents holstered their guns, and drew machetes instead - ones so sharp, they rang through the air just by being held.
	Connor and the Agents engaged in a brutal melee. The hostages scattered - some hopped the road barriers into the woodland nearby, others sprinted into the carriageway and futilely tried to flag down help.
	Chloe, Bea, and Anna helped Missy and Trey to their feet, rushing them to cover behind the bus. Missy rose, and couldn't help but peek over the window - wanting to see her brother in action.
	Meanwhile, Connor's fight grew in viciousness.
	"KILL! KILL! KILL!" the voice demanded. Connor grinned and nodded at the urge.
	An Agent's blade slashed Connor's torso, and hot blood poured from the wound. Connor didn't even flinch - he grinned. He delivered a knee to the Agent's gut, before headbutting him with the force of a speeding truck. The Agent stumbled back, and released his grip on the blade. Connor grabbed it, and in one slash, took off the Agent's head.
	The second Agent siezed the moment. He charged forward while Connor recovered, and drove his blade through his abdomen.
	Blood spat out from Connor's mouth. He morphed his mask so he could let it pour out rather than choke him.
	"NO!" Missy screamed, trying her utmost not to say "Connor!"
	But Connor wasn't done - far from it. His visor flashed red again - deeper, more savagely. He raised his arms out sideways, clenched his fists, and slammed them together on either side of the Agent's head.
	The sound was truly sickening - a mix of explosive force and bloody squelching. The Agent's head popped like a grape. His hands rose, trying in vain to locate his skull. Connor dug his hands into the now-open neck-stump, and pulled. In short order, the Agent's body was ripped in two halves - a gruesome tear running from neck to groin.
	The leader grimaced, realising he'd lost. He stood, and held his arms open.
	"Do your worst, then, traitor!" he dared.
	Connor sauntered over, and nonchalantly snapped the leader's neck - denying him the satisfaction of a grisly death.
	With that, Connor panted, absolutely soaked in blood. He gripped the machete's handle, and pulled, spraying gore all over the bus. He tore it from his torso, and dropped it on the ground.

	Finally, his friends came out from behind the bus. They went pale upon seeing the carnage.
	"Shit." Connor thought.
	"*Are... Are you all alright?*" he asked, putting on a stock American accent.
	"I... You... You're the Werewolf..." Chloe began, shocked.
	Missy looked up, and gave him a knowing nod.
	"Who are you?" Trey asked, panting.
	"I'm no one." Connor shook his head, still hiding his voice. "You're all safe now."
	He turned to leave.
	"Wait!" Chloe shouted. She approached Connor slowly, timidly, scared... but she could tell he wasn't there to hurt them.
	"You saved us... why?" she asked.
	Connor paused. "No. I killed these monsters. That's what I do. I'm... no-one's saviour."
	"You're wrong." Chloe replied, finding her voice. "You're our saviour. I don't know who you are, but I just want to say... thank you."
	Connor nodded, and leaped into the air, before running off.
	"What... What the hell was all that?!" Trey began, panting.
	"Fuck if I know..." Missy replied. "Is everyone okay?"
	"Yeah... I'm alright." Bea caught her breath.
	"I'm okay... are you alright?" Anna said, rushing to Missy.
	"I'm okay, baby..." Missy hugged her.
	"What was he doing here anyway?" Trey wondered, still in shock.
	"Who cares? If he hadn't shown up, we'd be dead. Maybe he's just... passing through?" Missy replied, covering.
	"I heard stories... rumours about that... thing. He... oh god, look at the bodies." Anna panted, her face pale.
	"Well... He did save us. Sure, it's grim, but... he saved our lives. And you saw how they fought - they were no more human than him." Bea countered.
	Chloe stood there, deep in thought.

	A half-hour passed. Connor used the time to clean himself of blood, and morph new clothes to hide his injuries.
	Sparky and Ivan arrived at his flat.
	"Hi dad! Did you have a big fight?" Sparky asked innocently, cleaning his jaws of blood.
	"Hah... big one, buddy." Connor chuckled. He looked up at Ivan.
	"That was no random act of violence, was it?" he asked.
	Ivan shook his head grimly.
	"What happend?" Sparky tilted his head.
	Connor took a deep breath.
	"ODESSA went after our friends. They stopped a bus, shot the driver, and beat up Trey and Missy."
	"Oh no! We have to go there now!" Sparky cried.
	"It's okay, buddy..." Connor sighed. "I killed the Agents. Still... we need to get there. I'll tell them I saw the attack on the news, and realised it was their bus."
	Ivan handed Connor a USB stick.
	"Found this on one of them. Can you take a look when you get a chance?" he asked.
	"Of course." Connor nodded.
	"Good man. Do svidaniya." Ivan smiled.

	Naismith stood outside the bus, the area cordoned off. FIs took photos of the mangled bodies.
	"So, to be clear..." he began, addressing the gang. "These assailants came aboard, attacked you--" he pointed at Trey and Missy, "And then they were killed by the Werewolf?"
	"That's correct, officer." Bea nodded confidently. Naismith stroked his chin.
	"Miss Derrington - do you think they were targeting you?" he asked.
	Chloe thought for a moment. "I don't think so. They never really threatened me specifically."
	"Still... they're the same kind of men we--" he caught himself. "Sorry, Miss Derrington - can I have a word in private?"
	Chloe nodded, and joined him away from the group.
	"These men..." he whispered. "They were superhumans - just like the ones your lab autopsies. Are you 100% *positive* they weren't here to harm you?"
	Chloe shrugged. "I'm a scientist, sir. I'm never 100% positive. But I don't think they were after me. The, um... the leader said 'Finally' when the Werewolf arrived - so I'm guessing we were just bait. Unlucky, I suppose."
	Naismith nodded. "Okay. Well, we'll be sending these ones to Morland too - I'm not too sure on the legality of having you autopsy them, but I'm sure your Legal department can hash that out."
	Chloe smiled faintly. Naismith headed to the group.
	"Okay everyone, you're free to go." he said. They thanked him, and left the cordon. There, Connor was arguing with a PC.
	"Please, my friends are in there!" he begged.
	"Sir, I'm afraid no-one from the public can enter until the officers have finished." the PC replied.
	Chloe rushed over, and embraced him. Sparky jumped up, and wrapped his paws around her. The rest of the group came over, and formed a mass-hug.
	As the group walked on, Trey went a little slower than the rest, deep in thought.
	Then, a terrible thought crossed his mind.
	"No..." he whispered to himself. "He can't be..."

	Back in the Captain's office, a terrified subordinate entered.
	"Sir, the squad... they all died." he began, gulping.
	"Good." the Captain leant forward. "If they died, they were weak. There is no room in the New Order for weaklings."
	"Yes, sir, Captain, sir." the subordinate stuttered. "This also confirms some of our earlier suspicions."
	"Agreed." the Captain nodded, his voice like gravel. "He took the bait far too quickly. For him to know immediately that a squad was sent out... It's the KGB."
	He paused, looking down at a dossier with pictures of Connor's friends. He chuckled slightly.
	"Let him think he's winning. Let him think he's free. Soon enough, he'll come crawling back. It is the nature of man to seek power."

	"I remember every single one." Connor replied grimly. "73. 26 normal humans, plus 47 Super-Agents."

	"And the normal people?"
	"Most of those, I wasn't in control at the time." Connor said clinically. "They were attacking me, and I got carried away and killed them instead of just injuring them. I haven't killed any normal humans since the 8th... there was an auction. Of kids." he continues.

	"Conspiracy?"
	"ODESSA." Connor answered grimly. "A cabal of former SS leaders, dedicated to re-starting the whole thing. Nazis, Trey. Nazis with god-damn superpowers."
	"Fuck..." Trey whispered, shuddering at the thought.
	Connor paused, the sadness evident on his face.
	"Trey, I... I wanted to tell you. And I was gonna. I just... I wanted to make sure that the worst of it was over." 
	"That wasn't your choice to make." Trey snapped. "They beat us all up while you were out doing god-knows-what - they did that to get to you, didn't they?"
	Connor nodded sadly.
	"Exactly. So, either way, we're involved. All you've done is ensure that we don't get any agency in that. You don't even let us know what kind of danger we're in!"
	Connor sat down, unable to reply.
	Trey sighed. He didn't want to keep arguing.
	"Look, I... I won't tell anyone." he said at last. "Just... Give me some time to process all this."
	Connor nodded, crying silently. He stood to leave.
	Trey wanted to hug Connor, but instead, closed the door. Connor stood there, and sobbed.

	Across the Atlantic, Connor sat on a high-end jetplane while an American man with a suit and an FBI badge briefed him.
	"Alright, so--" he began, revealing a map. "Murillo's a paranoid one. He's holed up in a compound out in Baja California - locals call it "La Villa del Lobo" - the Wolf's Villa. It's heavily guarded, and we believe his office is in the basement. The only way in is through the front door."

	"We'd ask that you keep casualties to a minimum, but as long as Murillo is dead, you'll get your payout." the man shrugged.

	The man nodded.
	"Off the record..." Connor began. "What's the FBI's interest in this? No offence, but you guys don't seem particularly interested in Central American prosperity."
	The man chuckled grimly. "Well, I'm FBI, not CIA. Besides, the State Department still has a vested interest in taking down Murillo. You're right, Mexico is our back yard - and Murillo doesn't wanna play ball. Instability like that is bad for business."
	Connor grinned. "So, it comes down to the Almighty Dollar after all."
	The man laughed, and they arrived on a private airfield in Baja California. They disembarked, and the man showed Connor to an ATV.
	"Buena caza, mi amigo." he grinned. Connor smirked, and drove onwards.

	Outside Murillo's compound, Connor stood menacingly. Two guards stood outside the front gate.
	"Hey!" one guard barked. "Que crees que estas haciendo aqui?!"
	Behind Connor's back, his suit morphed. A crossbow formed around his wrist, and loaded itself with a ball. Connor rose this, and fired right into the guard's head.
	The guard's eyes rolled back, and he collapsed to the ground, out cold. The other rushed to draw his gun, but the crossbow reloaded and redrew itself without delay. It fired, taking that one down too. He morphed up his costume, and re-created the ballistic shield from the bridge incident, before kicking the gate down.
	"MATALO!" a guard roared, as a hail of bullets came Connor's way. He ducked behind his shield, and thought for a second, before grinning. He morphed his crossbow throught the sheild - like a Roman ballista - and began shooting. He swapped his ammo out for makeshift Bolas - tangling the men onto the ground, gift-wrapped for the Federales.
	Women, drug dealers, and other civilians rushed out the gateway, as Connor continued through. Each shot of the bow sent another gunman down to the ground. Finally, the room went quiet, save the grunts and struggles of half-conscious gunmen.
	"Kill!" the voice in his head demanded, almost whining. Connor chuckled.
	He looked down, and realised his suit had gone thin - very thin. He used up most of its material making the Bolas, and would need time to regrow. Time he didn't have.
	He shrugged, and un-morphed the bow and shield, thickening his armour slightly. He headed down to the basement.
	There, Murillo sat, smoking a cigar at a desk. Two bodyguards opened fire, but Connor was a blur - taking both down in moments.
	"Ramon Murillo?" Connor asked, grinning.
	"Si." he nodded, taking a puff. He took out a pair of earmuffs. "Nos vemos en el infierno."
	Connor tilted his head, before realising. Murillo pressed a big red button, and an ultrasonic boom ripped through Connor's eardrums.
	He fell to the ground. The bodyguards woke from their torpor in agony, before going still, blood pouring from the noses and ears. Connor clutched his head, and tried to make it stop - but it wouldn't.
	Finally, an idea came to him, and he struggled. He used all his might to force his suit to change, and it did - two spikes, one on each index finger. He took a deep breath, and jammed them into his ears.
	The pain was awful, as he tore out his own inner ear. He screamed, but only felt the roar come from his throat - he heard nothing.
	"KILL!" the voice ordered. He heard *that.*
	He raised his claws. Murillo looked like he said "Puta madre!" but Connor couldn't tell. He swiped down, cleaving the desk in two. Murillo ducked out of the way, taking advantage of Connor's disorientation. He pressed a button, and Connor felt the vibrations stop on his skin - but nothing on his ears. Those were gone for now.
	He chased Murillo up the stairs like a wild animal. But as he reached the top, a new horror came.
	A Giant. Just like the ones in Belson. It grabbed him by the throat, and threw him out through the glass walls, sending him careening into the garden.
	Connor rose, and spat blood, before assuming a fighting stance. He shook his head, and braced.
	Then, another Giant came out.
	"Fuck..." Connor whispered--well, he probably shouted--"Two of them?!"
	The two walked towards him menacingly. He took a deep breath, and charged.
	The clash sent a shockwave that even Connor could hear. The two titans began beating Connor, as he beat them. No one was trying to block any attacks - they just wanted each other to die.
	One Giant grabbed Connor and held him, while the other freely pummeled him in the face.
	"Get off me... get *off* me..." Connor barked.
	"KILL! KILL THEM!" the voice howled. He felt his strength draw back into his body, and he closed his eyes.
	"GET OFF ME!" he roared. He *heard* the roar. His hearing was back.
	His visor glowed blood-red again. The Rage returned. He broke free, and barreled into one of them.
	He swiped with his claws like a rabid wildcat. The Giant put his guard up, but even that wasn't enough. Connor simply took advantage of the size difference, and clawed at the Giant's belly, disemboweling him.
	Then, he turned, ripping open the second one's tendons and armour. It raised him up, and bashed him into the wall, leaving cracked bricks and concrete dust. Connor responded by morphing his leg-armour into a blade, and sliced open the Giant's forearm. It howled in agony, and Connor finished the job - a blade to the throat, going through and taking out the spinal column. He grinned at last, and swiped, beheading the monster.
	Connor stood there, panting, exhausted. The last Giant, clutched his bowels, and roared. The two met, their fists connecting with each other's heads. They both fell, and Connor got up. The Giant didn't.
	Connor walked forwards, before falling to his knees. With that, the Federales arrived on the scene. They saw the sights and were horrified. Connor fell, unable to retain consciousness.

	A few hours later, he awoke. He was back on the plane, heading back. The FBI man went pale upon seeing him rise.
	"You... you're okay..." he stammered.
	Connor shrugged. "Seems so. Did Murillo get away?"
	"No." the man shook his head. "The Federales caught him, and we intervened, taking him into our custody."
	"He's with ODESSA..." Connor noted grimly.
	"I don't think so." the man shrugged. "Your friend in the KGB sent me the report on the last 8-foot freak you tangled with. Seems like these two were different."
	"Different how?"
	"Well for starters, they were both locals. Needless to say, here in the US, ODESSA ain't exactly fond of Mexicans. Second, we haven't done a full autopsy - but looking at the difference, it seems these two weren't anywhere near as tough. They said they needed bonesaws just to break the last one's skin - but the boys in Quantico have had no such trouble. These jokers were made as an imitation. Explains why you needed help killing one in the past, but you could take down two today."
	Connor stroked his chin, deep in thought. "We on our way back?" he finally asked.
	"Yeah. We're just arriving at DC now." the man nodded. "From there, you'll get a plane to Edinburgh, and then from there to Drackhill."
	Connor smiled. "And the money?"
	"Look who cares about Almighty Dollar now." the man smirked. "Yeah, the money's been wired. Don't spend it all at once."
	Connor chuckled, and they landed in DC.

	Connor approached one - there were no signs of his face on this one. It must have been even further degenerated than the first. He looked at the notes next to it.
	"Clones. Of me. Grown from my hand." Connor said, clinically. The human boy they took and twisted would be sickened - but Connor was used to these horrors by now. Hell, only in the past week did he strangle a man with his own entrails - this was getting old.
	"I... What? No, your hand was... was incinerated. As soon as I was done studying it, I passed it over to the lab who said they incinerated it..." Chloe said, mortified.
	"Clearly, they lied." Connor replied. "The first subject was more like me - less... grotesque. These ones... they must have been cultured from its tissue. A flawed copy of a flawed copy. Poor wretches." 
	"This... this isn't just cloning." Chloe began. "The degeneration, the malformed tissue - it's as if they were trying to replicate something without understanding the underlying biology. Each iteration seems weaker, more unstable. I've seen something like this in genetic studies before, but nothing this extreme."
	Connor put his hand up to the glass of one cage.
	"Kill me... kill me..." the creature begged. Connor gasped. A flash hit his mind like a train - memories. The drills, the saws, the syringes... The old man laughing. The agony... The same agony this creature felt. For a moment, he wasn't in the lab anymore - he was back there. The drills screeched in his ears. Blades carved into flesh. A cruel laugh echoed in the darkness. Never again."

	She approached the notes on one specimen, and read them. "These clones... they're genetically modified, but they haven't been allowed to develop naturally. Instead of growing and maturing like normal cells, they're being forcefully accelerated. It's causing rapid mutations, which explains the grotesque appearance and the pain response. They're not just victims of bad science; they're experiments gone wrong. Whoever is running this operation doesn't care about ethical boundaries, or human life for that matter."
	"I agree. They..." he said, glancing back at the notes. "They've been injected with radioactive compounds to limit their healing powers. That means they can be overdosed. Here--" he pointed to the pain relief button - "Go to the others. Hold that button down for 10 seconds, and it'll deliver a dosage high enough to kill them."
	Chloe gulped - the idea of killing them herself was offputting.	But she steeled herself, and did it.
	"They need this. It's wrong." she whispered, and held down the button, her eyes closed. She reopened them, and saw a misshapen, misplaced, discoloured eye from the creature look back at her - was it thanking her?
	Connor did the same, and in less than a minute, the poor wretches all stopped quivering.

	Connor paused. He pushed the button, incinerating the bodies of the creatures, and the pair headed further down - into a storage zone.

	She tilted her head, studying him. "You're... different to what I expected." she said softly. "There's... something familiar about you. The way you move. The way you talk. It's almost like..."

SCENE
	Connor ascended the stairs, taking a moment to un-morph his mask and wipe his nose. The bullet to the head didn't crack his skull, but it still hurt. He took a deep breath, re-morphed his mask, and headed up to the rooftop. There, he saw the Agent, clad in armour and Swastika icons, pointing his gun at Chloe.

	The Agent sneered, clearly rattled but not broken. He straightened, and chuckled darkly. "Hah... Nice try."

The ground beneath them seemed to tremble as the force of his words resonated. "+*THE WRATH... IS _MINE ALONE_!*+"
	With a primal roar, he charged. He threw a punch with such force that the air seems to crack around it. The Agent barely managed to block, but the impact sent him sliding back. Connor pressed the attack, launching another punch, then a devastating uppercut that could take a human's head off. Each swing felt like it could tear through steel, each blow a promise of death.
	Chloe looked on, horrified and transfixed by the scene. But only one thought was in her mind.

	"Kill... Kill... Kill..." the voice groaned, spurring him onwards.

The Agent screamed as the blades cut across his face, sending a spray of blood into the air. He staggered back, but Connor followed, relentless.
	He gripped the blade from his chest. He had to finish this. He had to save Chloe.
	"KILL!" the voice roared, spurring him on. His constant humming migraine faded for a moment - even his flesh wanted this man dead.
	He pulled the blade from his chest, as the Agent jumped on his back. He ran himself through, impaling both.
	For a moment, there was silence, save for the ragged breaths of two men on the verge of death. Blood pooled around them, dark and thick.
	They both fell away from each other, and struggled to stand up, blood pouring from their chests and mouths. Connor planted the blade in the ground, and used it to help him stand.
	Chloe rushed to him, her eyes wide with horror and relief. She helped him to his feet, but just as they thought they had a moment of calm, the Agent drew his gun again, aiming it directly at her head. 
	"Ah ah ah!" the Agent laughed. He motioned for Chloe to step away, and she reluctantly did so. Connor growled, like a true Werewolf.
	The Agent approached and grabbed her, holding the gun to her head.
	"Nice try. But the heart always was your weakness, traitor." he laughed. "On your knees."
	Connor sank down. 
	"Now..." the Agent smirked. "Take off your mask."
	Connor shuddered. Chloe gulped.
	"No... Don't... It... it can't be..." she stammered, knowing deep down what she'd see. "I don't want to know." she whispered. "Don't be Connor... Don't be Connor..."
	"Oh, but it is. Come on, traitor. Listen and Obey." the Agent grinned.
	Connor slowly raised his hands, and pulled down his mask. The colour drained from Chloe's face as she saw him.
	"...Connor?" she asked, choking back tears.
	"I... I'm sorry..." he admitted, unable to look her in the eyes.
	"See him! See how he lies, like the duplicitous Jew! The wayward son of our master. Misbegotten. A failure. You were meant to be one of us, Connor! A perfect specimen. How dare you betray your own kind!" the Agent laughed.
	With that, Chloe sprang into action. Remembering Connor's training, she grabbed the Agent's wrist, launched his arm into the air, and shoved. His grip was too tight for him to let go of the gun, but he stumbled, towards the edge of the roof.
	"Filthy cripple!" he roared, aiming his gun at her.
	"NO!" Connor bellowed, launching himself.
	The Agent pulled the trigger just a second before Connor slammed into his torso. Both men careened off the edge. The bullet barely missed Chloe, grazing her cheek, adding a cut to her old scar.
	She froze for a moment. As the two fell, the Agent shot at Connor in the air. Chloe ran to the edge, and saw them hit the ground together. A thud... a sickening thud. She fell to her knees.
	"Connor... CONNOR!" she screamed.
	She ran down the stairs, as fast as her legs can took her. She heard gunshots - the police had swarmed the building now, to rescue the hostages. She'd have to be quick...
	She darted past them, and found her way to the alleyway Connor landed. The same alleyway he and Sparky saved her from all those months ago. There, she saw the Agent - or what was left of him. He landed right on his head, and a pile of red mush was all that remained above his neck.
	But Connor... Connor landed back-first on a dumpster. He was bent backwards in a sickening, unnatural way - his back was snapped clean in half. Chloe fell down to her knees again.
	"No... NO!" she sobbed. She pulled his body from the dumpster, laying him down flat. He didn't breathe.
	"Connor... Connor, wake up. Come on, wake up. Please wake up... Hey, remember this alleyway? You saved me here, and you just saved me again. Come on... Come on, get up! That's an order!" she pleaded. She slammed his chest with her fist, causing a cracking noise from his spine.
	"Come on, get up... Hey, if you get up, I'll... I'll forgive you, okay? I won't be mad, not even a little. Just... please wake up. You've survived so much, you can survive this! Please!" she sobbed. "Please..." she begged, as she hit his chest again. Another cracking noise. With that...
	"GAAGGH!" Connor gasped, his eyes shooting open.
	"Connor?!" she looked up.
	"Agh.. AAAGH!" he screamed in agony. He rolled onto his front and clutched his back.
	"Connor... Connor, what... What do I do?" she asked, tears streaming down her cheek.
	"Agh... Ah... I... Help..." he spluttered out, trying to stand. Chloe helped him up. He shouted in pain as he rose, but found his footing.
	"Connor, you... You're alive..." she whispered, in shock.
	With that, the police exited the building. "Area secure, sir!" Nina barked. "All hostages save one have been located. Captive hostile has been subdued."
	"I..." Chloe began. "You'd better go. If they find you..."
	"Chloe, I..." Connor started, but she raised her hand, silencing him.
	"We'll talk about this later, okay? I... I'll see you later." she said, and hugged him. Though his back was in agony, he hugged her too, and hobbled off into the distance.

Maybe they wanted to see how much they could give someone without killing them. Anyway, they got more than they bargained for. I am to them what they are to humans."

	"The Super-Agents, because there's no safe way to let them live. The humans... most of them were collateral damage. I was lost in the Rage, and they were attacking me - it was instinct. There are 3 normal humans I killed of my own free will." Connor explained, studying her reaction. "Omar Hattab - a Moroccan general plotting a war. Alan Hughes - a perv who sold kids. And Vadim Zamaldayev - a Chechen warlord."

	"I didn't want to kill them. But when you're forced into a corner, when they give you no choice... it's not always as clear-cut as we want it to be."

	"Sparky - stay here. If any of these bastards come for Chloe, you know what to do."
	"Rip them apart." Sparky growled. Chloe looked over at Sparky, and hugged him tightly.
	Connor morphed his suit and went out.

	"So... You can talk?" she finally asked.
	"Yes! I'm sorry you can't understand me, but I can talk!" he barked happily.
	"Hah... I don't know what that was, but it sounded happy." she mused.

	"Ah, is that a no?" Chloe asked. Sparky nodded.
	"Hah... at least we can talk now, eh buddy?" Chloe smiled. She hugged him tight.
	Sparky looked at her.
	"I did tell him one thing." he said, smirking.
	"What's that? Did you tell him something?" Chloe asked, piecing it together somewhat.
	Sparky nodded.
	"What did you tell him?"

	While seated and taking in some fresh air, blood came from his nostrils. He'd been overdoing it today - two near-death experiences. His Paradrenaline was burning through his body. He sighed, pulled out his lighter, and began to burn his wrist. The pain was sharp, but it soon gives way to relief. The migraines subsided, the nosebleed stopped, and even the burn felt nice.

I get migraines, nosebleeds, seizures even. Normally, that just knocks me into this... coma-thingy. I can't describe it well, but it's like my body switches off to repair. But when I'm really exhausted, the migraines get unbearable. And the only way to prevent them is... acute pain. Like burns." he said, gesturing to his arm. "It only works like this - it's gotta be very acute, very localised. Otherwise it just adds to the headache."

	Chloe swallowed, and hugged Connor. He returned the embrace.
	"You know..." she began, "I studied your Paradrenaline - I knew these side-effects would occur from overdosage, but... pain, acute pain, lessening the symptoms?"
	"I don't know - it was Sparky who taught me." he shrugged.
	"It must be an endorphin thing..." she mused.
	He smiled softly. She gave him a sad smile, and yawned.
	"You can take the bed, it's fine." he nodded.
	"I'm not the one who got killed twice." she quipped.
	He chuckled. "Touche."

	"Absolutely. And I... I want you to know, you... you have every right to be pissed off."
	She smiled softly. "I'll see you in the morning, yeah?"
	"Yeah, I'll... I'll see you then."

SCENE
	That night, Connor was sprinting, leaping from rooftop to rooftop in a patrol. While running, he heard a scream. He sprinted straight towards the source.

	The creature turned slowly, its face twisted into a grotesque grin. But what really threw Connor off is the voice - a refined, cultured tone that seemed out of place for something so monstrous. "Greetings, Heretic." it growled, lips curling. "Are you ready for your judgment?"
	Connor raised an eyebrow, taking a step forward. His usual cocky smirk formed. "Who the fuck are you?"
	"I am the Judge." the creature replied, showing its teeth, the grin stretching impossibly wide. "And I am your end, Heretic."

	The Judge's grin faltered for a moment, but then it returned, colder than before. "Such insolence, to curse and demean your natural father. Your death has been demanded - thus sayeth the Lord."
	"'The Lord'? You mean the Captain?" Connor asked, eyebrow raised.
	"Do not dare blaspheme in such ways." the Judge snarled, his voice venomous. "To compare the Lord to the Captain is to compare a star to a single ember."
	Connor tilted his head, genuinely curious now. "Who were you? What, a preacher?"
	The Judge's eyes narrowed, a cold flicker passing through them. "I am not here as a preacher. Though my words are Truth Primordial, I do not come to bring the Word to the deaf ears of Man. I am the Judge. And I find you... guilty."
	His voice hardened, and his grip tightened on his weapons.

	The Judge's eyes flared. "Be silent." he snapped, his voice sharp. "Mine eyes have been opened, Heretic. Do not dare labour under the false illusion that you can close them once more."
	Connor stared at him, his expression hardening. "Have it your way." he muttered, his eyes flashing. He morphed his blades, their gleaming edges catching the light. "Let's dance."

	Without another word, they charged.
	"Kill! Kill! Kill!" the voice chanted encouragingly.

	The sound of their blades clashing rang out in the alley as the two monsters collided. The first thing Connor noticed was the Judge's strength - far greater than he expected. The creature moved with unnatural speed, his strikes heavy and relentless. Connor was forced to backpedal, his blades deflecting each blow.
	The Judge struck again, and this time, Connor's parry was too slow. The Judge's blade cut deep into Connor's thigh. Blood poured from the wound.
	Connor swung his blade with a growl, his edge slicing across the Judge's thigh. The creature howled in pain, stumbling back slightly, but the grin never left its face.
	The Judge's next move was swift - he brought his blade down toward Connor's head. Connor reacted instinctively, diving backward, barely avoiding the blow. He threw a knife, but the creature was too fast, parrying the blade with one of its own. The two made eye contact - two predators circling each other, their blades hungry for blood.
	"About time for a challenge." Connor thought, the adrenaline surging through him. His fear was buried deep, hidden beneath the hunger for battle.
	The Judge didn't waste time. He plunged his blade into the ground, sending a shockwave of energy through the earth. The pavement cracked, and gravel flew into the air. With a growl, the Judge charged forward, sweeping his blade up. The gravel cut into Connor's eyes, blinding him momentarily.
	Connor staggered back, wiping the dirt from his eyes, but the Judge was already on him. The second flurry of strikes came fast, and one of them finally landed - cutting across Connor's abdomen. The pain was immediate, sharp, and deep. Blood poured from the wound, but Connor forced himself to focus.
	With a roar, he swung his longblade, the strike strong enough to send a shockwave through the Judge's defenses. The creature blocked the attack, but Connor grinned. It was a feint. He thrusted his shortblade forward, burying it deep into the Judge's abdomen.
	But the Judge didn't falter. His grin only grew wider as he grabbed Connor's blade and pushed it out, his other hand moving faster than Connor could react. In a single fluid motion, the Judge morphed his blades into a spear, thrusting it toward Connor. The weapon drove into his abdomen with brutal force.
	Connor grabbed the spear, pulling himself toward the Judge with a snarl. He morphed blades from his wrists, slashing at the Judge's face. The strike connected, cutting deep, but the Judge simply grinned. He twisted the spear, and Connor felt the blade tear through his insides, sending shockwaves of agony through his body.
	For the first time since starting his quest, real, primal fear crept into Connor's heart. The blood loss, the agony, the damage...
	"Kill him! Kill him! Kill him!" the voice begged, the fear in it palpable.
	Thoughts of Chloe, Sparky, Trey, Missy, Anna, Bea, and Vince flooded his mind. His family. His friends. He couldn't die here. Not like this.
	The Judge morphed his spear back into twin blades, spinning them in the air like a tornado of death. Connor tried to stand his ground, but his legs betrayed him. He was on the edge of collapse.
	Then, with a deafening howl, Connor's eyes flashed red. Rage. The bloodlust took over, drowning out the pain, drowning out the fear. His body surged with raw power, and his vision turns crimson.
	The Judge wiped blood from his mouth, his grin widening. "Now... Now it's a fight." he muttered, his own eyes flashing red with a sudden, dangerous fury. He un-morphed his blades, drawing wristblades in their place.
	The two monsters collided again. Their wristblades clashed in a shower of sparks, neither one attempting to block - only strike. Blood splattered across the alley as their bodies were torn. For a moment, the Judge stumbled, his left hand pressing against the stab wound Connor inflicted earlier. But his grin only grew fiercer, and his eyes glowed red.
	For a split second, Connor's mind cleared. "He can Rage too?" The thought barely registered before his beastly instincts took over once more. The two continued to clash, a blur of violence and blood.
	The Judge hit harder than anyone Connor had faced before. Each strike felt like it could shatter bone, and Connor was barely able to stay on his feet. But he fought through the pain, launching a haymaker that connected with the Judge's ribcage. He felt something crack beneath his fist.
	For a moment, the Judge faltered, his breath ragged. He straightened, his body obeying his will with terrifying precision.
	Connor didn't realize his mistake until it was too late.
	The Judge swiped, his blade slashing across Connor's throat with terrifying precision. Before he could react, the Judge grabbed his tongue, yanking it out with a sickening pull.
	Then, in one fluid motion, the Judge re-morphed his spear, driving it through Connor's heart.
	Connor howled, the sound tearing from his chest as the spear twisted, shredding his lungs. Blood poured from him in torrents as the Judge raised the spear into the air, a triumphant roar echoing in the alley.
	With a brutal, final motion, the Judge drove the spear into the ground, impaling Connor like a trophy.
	Connor's limp body slumped to the ground, blood pooling around him. The Judge stood over him, his eyes returning to their cold, fanatical calm. He chuckled, the sound dark and victorious.
	"This is the Litany of Blood." he began, before kneeling and offering a prayer to his delusions.

	With that, the Judge rose, bowed, and left.
	Connor's limp, apparently lifeless body slid down the spear, making a sickening *squelch* as it hit the ground.
	Must hold on. Must hold on.
	"Hold on..." the voice echoed.
	Every cell in Connor's body screamed. Every nerve ending begged him to just let them die.
	Must hold on. Must hold on.
	"Hold on..."
	No oxygen. Only backup hearts for circulation.
	Must hold on. Must hold on.
	"Hold on..."
	Bleeding from every organ. Brain... shutting down...
	Must... hold on...
	"Hold... On..."

I can't explain it, but while you were in the coma, your muscle density nearly doubled. Maybe, when you suffer near-fatal trauma, your body rebuilds itself stronger than before."

	"I mean, your non-essential cells entered dormant states to avoid using up energy - and, for the record, the cells your body considers 'non-essential' is pretty revealing on its own. Practically everything except your amygdala, your backup hearts, and your bone marrow, was all shut down. The lactic acid buildup you had - it would have caused any human cell to enter apoptosis almost immediately. But yours just kept on going. You've, um... You've had some damage to the amygdala, but that's mostly healed now. Still, your reflexes and motor control will be impaired somewhat."
	"And the hole in my chest?" Connor asked.

	"Connor..." she began.
	"Guys... can you give me and Chloe a minute?" Connor asked. Ivan and Sparky nodded and left.

I hate lying to them." she admitted. "The ones who know about you, know. We've been meeting up regularly. They haven't come in - doing so might blow your cover. I just..."

	"I hate that I understand why you do this. I hate that I see the person you are - the person who would sacrifice everything to protect others - and I know I'd never ask you to change. I wish you never got these powers of yours - but you do have them. And that means you have a responsibility to use them. And if you weren't the kind of guy to feel that way, then I probably never would have fallen in---" she caught herself. It was harder to spit it out when he was awake. "...Fallen for you. But it doesn't make this any easier, Connor." she said. "I'm torn. I feel angry that you're out there risking your life, guilty for me being so selfish... When I'm with you, I feel... I feel like I'm keeping you away from the people who need you, who *really* need you. But... *I* need you! And I'm useless to you."

	"I..." Chloe began. "I just feel so powerless watching you fight, knowing I can only help from the sidelines. I can't fight these things! I can study you, but what good am I from here?"
	"I have an idea." Connor tilted his head. "I know what you're like - you took a look at the paradrenaline in my system, right?"
	"Yeah - I was trying to find a way to stimulate it to help you heal quicker." she replied.
	"And did you find anything else?"
	"I... yes!" Chloe said, realising. "Hang on..." 
	She went through the notes she'd taken through the process. "Here! The endorphin-analogue that counteracts the paradrenaline. Your body kept almost rinsing your head with it - thank god it did, or you'd have had a seizure, or worse. In fact, I think this substance is what puts you in the healing coma."
	"That's the substance that counters the paradrenaline? And can you synthesise more of it?"
	"Yes - in a couple hours, I could make a full dose." Chloe replied.
	Realisation dawned on Connor's face. "The Judge will be out again in a few hours. Before we head out, can you make enough paradrenaline to trigger the Rage? And... a full dose of the endorphins?"
	"Yeah, absolutely. I'll crack on now." Chloe said, brushing away her tears and squaring her shoulders.
	Connor rose, a soft smile breaking through the pain on his face. He pulled Chloe into a hug, holding her tightly. She returned the embrace, not wanting it to end.
	She swallowed hard, resting her forehead against his. "Rest while you can. I'll handle this."
	Connor nodded, stepping back. As he laid back down, Chloe sat at her makeshift lab station, her hands trembling for only a moment before she steadied them. She glanced back at him, then down at her notes. Her jaw set with quiet determination.

	"I know what you mean. I mean, I know you were staying round mine while we waited for the heat to die down, but... I really liked cuddling you at night." Connor replied, blushing slightly.
	Chloe smiled, and kissed him.
	She pulled back, and put her hand on his heart. He put his hand over hers, and squeezed tightly.
	"It's still there, then?" he asked, smirking.
	"How many hearts do you have now?" she quipped, raising an eyebrow.
	"Oof... At least 5 last time I checked." Connor replied nonchalantly. "So, on the plus side, you can break it 4 times and I'll be fine."
	They chuckled. She looked into his eyes, and blushed.
	Time seemed to slow down for them.
	"It's funny, isn't it?" Connor began. "We've only known each other for 6 months, and yet..."
	"...it feels like longer, doesn't it?" she finished his sentence. Connor smiled warmly.
	"I should have asked you out *way* sooner." he smirked.
	"Yeah, you should have." she grinned.
	"If it helps, I consider our walk with Sparky to be our first date."
	"Really? Lame. I consider meeting in the library to be our first." she quipped back.
	Connor laughed. "You know... I'm not gonna lie, I had a crush on you since we met back then."
	Chloe smiled, and blushed. "I had one on you too."
	"Probably why it feels like we've known each other longer. We've practically been dating without realising."
	Chloe chuckled. "Well, in that case, I'm the one who approached you in the library - so technically, I asked you out."
	"Oh yeah? Well... Nah, I've got no comeback for that."
	Chloe leant into him, and closed her eyes for a moment, enjoying it.
	"Chloe, I..." he began. Chloe looked at him, her eyes fluttering slightly.
	Connor steeled himself. "I love you." he said.
	For a moment, time froze. Chloe's eyes widened.
	Then, she smiled - a wide, warm smile. She pulled him in, and kissed him. The two held each other in the kiss for as long as they could hold their breath.
	Finally, they pulled apart.
	"I love you too." she said, and hugged him tightly.

However, Vincent claimed to have strongarmed the boy into joining him, and so no charges were brought - and, crucially, no DNA samples were taken. Despite this, Connor has made a few visits to HMP Wickermast over the last few months."

At age 8, he discovered that his foster father was molesting his sister, and he killed him. He and his foster sister were then re-homed by Vincent, who raised them both from then on."

	"I know. I'll see you soon, boy." the Captain growls, before hanging up.
